research.summary: 18Birdies has no public API, no developer or partner program, and no MCP server of its own. No community MCP server can read live 18Birdies data either. There is one supported way to get the data out: the self-serve "Download Your Account Data" page at https://18birdies.com/download-account-data/. You sign in on the web with email and password, or with a phone number and SMS code. The page then immediately downloads 18Birdies_archive.json, which holds every round you have played (the help center describes this page, updated July 2, 2026). For each round the archive has: a round id, a timestamp in milliseconds, the club's UUID and name, total strokes, score relative to par, an array of 9 or 18 per-hole stroke counts, and round-level totals (birdie/par/bogey counts, fairway hit and miss direction, GIR and miss direction, total putts). It does NOT have per-hole par, per-hole putts, per-hole fairway or GIR, tee played, course rating or slope, shots, or in-app notes. Per-hole par, stroke index, yardage and tee rating/slope are public on 18Birdies' club pages, which are keyed by the same club UUID the archive uses; I checked this with a real UUID from an archive. That makes enrichment possible, but only by hand or for a few courses, because the Terms of Service ban automated scraping. So the realistic "tap into 18Birdies" design is: (1) download the export by hand, which is sanctioned and gives the full history each time; (2) feed it into your own local SQLite or Parquet store; (3) optionally put your own local MCP server on top of that store. Screenshots plus a vision model are then only needed for per-hole putts, fairways and GIR on the rounds you care about. You could script the site's two web calls (login, then getMyData) to download the export automatically, but those calls are undocumented and the Terms of Service forbid "automated means" unless expressly authorized, so that is your call. Several other routes are weak or not viable: Strava (since June 2026: only new public rounds, totals only, subscriptions required, AI use banned on the API), GHIN (18Birdies does not sync with it), Apple Health or Garmin (no scores), and reverse-engineering the mobile API (ToS §8.9 forbids it, and no public prior work exists).

options.name: 1. Official account-data export (18Birdies_archive.json), downloaded by hand
options.how_it_works: Go to https://18birdies.com/download-account-data/ in a desktop or phone browser and sign in (email+password, or phone number + SMS code). Click 'Request My Data'. The page's JS POSTs to https://18birdies.com/usercentral/api/user/getMyData with the session token and saves the response straight away as 18Birdies_archive.json; there is no email and no waiting. The export is a full snapshot every time, so you can re-download whenever you like (e.g., monthly or after a batch of rounds) and ingest idempotently keyed on round id. The help center points users to this page ('request or download an archive of your 18Birdies account data'). The site's own UI calls it an archive that includes 'activities, photos, posts, rounds and more'.
options.data_obtained: Top level is myData with these sections: accountData (userId, userName, registerTimestamp, birthYear, email, mobileNumber, which is PII), activityData {roundCount, rounds[]}, clubData {playedClubs[{clubId,name}], postedInClubs}, feedData {messages[{messageId, content?}]}, friendData, subscriptionData. Each round has: id, timestamp (epoch ms), clubId{id} (facility UUID), strokes (gross), score (to par, so total par = strokes - score), holeStrokes (int array of length 9 or 18, 0 = hole not played). It also has a stats object with aces, doubleEagleOrBetter, eagles, birdies, pars, bogeys, doubleBogeyOrWorse, fairwayLefts/Middles/Rights/Shorts/Longs, fairwayHoleCount, gir, girLefts/Rights/Shorts/Longs, girNoChances, girHoleCount, putts, puttHoleCount, strokeGainOverall/TeeToGreen (both 100 = sentinel for not available), and recommendedStats[{type: FAIRWAY_HIT_PERCENTAGE|GIR_PERCENTAGE|TOTAL_PUTTS, value}]. NOT included: per-hole par, per-hole putts/FIR/GIR/penalties, tee name, rating/slope, which course at a multi-course facility, shots/GPS, 18Birdies hole/course Notes, handicap history, weather. Data-quality notes from a public example archive (75 rounds, Jul 2021 to Dec 2025): 7 rounds were all zeros (abandoned), 19 were partial, in 8 sum(holeStrokes) != strokes, and puttHoleCount was 0 even when putts > 0.
options.effort: Very low. About 1 minute per download plus a roughly 100-line pandas parser. Existing parsers such as chrisdecali/golf-reports ingest/pull_18birdies.py and mfannin099 read_json_pandas.py are useful as schema references only; nothing needs to be installed.
options.risks: None under the ToS, since this is a first-party feature. Privacy: the file contains your email, phone, birth year, friends list and feed posts. Keep the raw file out of git (gitignore data/raw/) and never publish it via GitHub Pages; publish only aggregates. Schema risk: it is undocumented and could change without notice, so validate with Pydantic and fail loudly. The newest public sample I found was generated Dec 2025, and a June 2026 parser used the same keys; that the current export still matches is likely but not verified with a fresh 2026 file.

options.name: 2. Scripted export using the website's own two calls (semi-official automation)
options.how_it_works: Reproduce what the download page does in Python: POST https://18birdies.com/usercentral/api/user/userLogin with JSON {account, password} (or {account, verificationCode, alpha2Code} after POST /usercentral/api/user/sendVerificationCode for phone logins). The response contains a token. Then POST https://18birdies.com/usercentral/api/user/getMyData with body {} and the header 'Token: <token>'. This could run weekly or nightly in GitHub Actions with credentials stored as secrets, matching your usual pipeline pattern. I read these calls from the site's JS; I did not run them.
options.data_obtained: Same as option 1 (the full archive JSON).
options.effort: Low: roughly 30 lines of requests code plus a secret. Token lifetime is unknown. Not practical if your account uses phone + SMS login, because each run would need a new SMS code.
options.risks: ToS gray area. The Terms (last updated Jan 29, 2021) ban 'web crawler, spidering or other automated means to access, copy, index, process and/or store any Content... other than as expressly authorized by us in writing'. The export is a user-facing feature, but scripting it is not expressly authorized. Other risks: the endpoints are undocumented and may change or add bot checks; you would be storing your 18Birdies password in CI secrets; unusual login patterns could trigger account flags (unconfirmed). If you choose this, run it infrequently. The safer alternative is a reminder that prompts you to download by hand.

options.name: 3. Course enrichment from public club scorecard pages (keyed by the archive's clubId)
options.how_it_works: Each archive round carries clubId.id, a UUID. https://18birdies.com/golf-courses/club/<clubId>/<any-slug> is a public, server-rendered page with the club's scorecard: per-hole Par, Handicap (stroke index), and yardage per tee, plus rating/slope per tee (e.g., 'White (126/68.2)'). I confirmed that a clubId taken from a real archive resolves to the right club page (HTTP 200 with any slug). Joining this with holeStrokes gives per-hole score to par, par-3/4/5 scoring averages, and scoring by stroke index. The public handicap calculator also calls an unauthenticated /usercentral/api/course/getClub2 {clubId} that returns tees, per-hole teeYardages and per-tee slope/rating arrays (tsls/tcrs); whether it returns par is unconfirmed.
options.data_obtained: Per club: courses, per-hole par and stroke index, yardage per tee, course rating and slope per tee and gender. Gaps: the archive never says which tee you played or which course at a multi-course facility, so rating/slope and 27-hole layouts need a one-time mapping from you (e.g., 'home course = Blue tees').
options.effort: Low if you do it by hand (or with a one-off screenshot and the vision API) for the handful of clubs you play. It is a small per-course YAML/CSV you maintain.
options.risks: Fetching these pages with a script is scraping under the ToS clause, so keep it manual, or use a licensed course-data source instead (e.g., the GolfCore MCP 'Scorecards, tee yardages, USGA ratings' listed in the official MCP registry; quality and terms unverified). Do not bulk-crawl.

options.name: 4. Build your own local MCP server over the ingested export (the realistic 'MCP' answer)
options.how_it_works: No 18Birdies MCP exists, so write a small Python FastMCP server (stdio) that reads your local golf.db (built from options 1 and 3, plus screenshot extractions and your notes timeline). Register it in Claude Desktop or Claude Code. Tools could include import_archive(path), list_rounds(since, club), get_round(round_id), trends(window), timeline(start, end), compare_periods(event_id, n_before, n_after). This is how chrisdecali/golf-reports handles 18Birdies: its import_18birdies(archive_path) tool only parses the export; it has no live access.
options.data_obtained: Whatever is in your store: all export fields, plus course enrichment, screenshot-derived per-hole stats, and lesson/practice events.
options.effort: Low to medium: about 150 lines using the official MCP Python SDK.
options.risks: None beyond local file hygiene. Do not install or run the third-party golf-reports repo; it has 0 stars, no license, is from June 2026, and also handles Arccos/GHIN credentials. Use it only as a design reference.

options.name: 5. Screenshot / 'Share Scorecard' image + vision LLM (complement, not replacement)
options.how_it_works: In the app: Me > Rounds > a round > Share Scorecard produces a shareable scorecard that you can send through the iOS share sheet (email, Files, etc.). Round History, scorecards and stats can only be viewed in the mobile app; there is no web app. Screenshots of the full scorecard or stats screens are the only non-reverse-engineered way to get per-hole putts, FIR and GIR. Use the export as the backbone (dates, clubs, hole strokes for every round) and screenshots only for the per-hole detail on the rounds you want. The export's holeStrokes can serve as a checksum on the vision output.
options.data_obtained: Whatever is visible on screen, typically per-hole par, strokes and putts, and possibly fairway/GIR markers if you track them. The exact format of the shared scorecard (image vs link) is unconfirmed.
options.effort: Covered by the separate screenshot-extraction area.
options.risks: Manual step per round. Vision errors can be reconciled against the export's holeStrokes and strokes.

options.name: 6. Strava bridge (18Birdies -> Strava -> Strava API or Strava MCP)
options.how_it_works: Since June 16, 2026, 18Birdies can auto-post completed rounds to Strava (Me > ... > Connected Apps & Devices > Strava). Only rounds finished after you connect are posted, and only if round visibility is 'Everyone'. Older rounds can be shared manually one at a time. The Strava activity includes course name and location, gross score, counts of birdies, pars and bogeys, round duration, and an end-of-round summary graphic with your scorecard. You would read it back through Strava's official MCP connector (launched June 1, 2026; Strava subscribers only; Claude only; read-only; whether it exposes activity descriptions or photos is unconfirmed) or through the Strava API.
options.data_obtained: Per future round: date/time, duration, course, gross score, birdie/par/bogey counts, and a scorecard image. No historical backfill, and totals only unless you run vision on the image.
options.effort: Medium, for less data than the export.
options.risks: Strava's 2026 API Policy requires a paid Strava subscription for Standard-tier developers and bans using Strava API data 'in connection with the development, training, evaluation, or operation of any AI Application'. That conflicts with running a vision LLM on the scorecard image pulled through the API. Only the Strava MCP is allowed for personal AI use. Your rounds would also need to be public in 18Birdies. Useful at most as a 'new round played' signal. Not recommended.

research.design_notes:
## Recommended ingestion path (ranked)
1. **Primary:** download `18Birdies_archive.json` by hand (option 1) → `data/raw/18birdies/18Birdies_archive_<YYYYMMDD>.json` (gitignored) → parse → `golf.db` (SQLite) or Parquet.
2. **Enrichment:** a hand-maintained `courses.yaml` (per clubId: course name, tee you usually play, per-hole par and stroke index, rating/slope), filled once per club from the public page `https://18birdies.com/golf-courses/club/<clubId>/x` or from one screenshot run through the vision API.
3. **Per-hole detail (optional):** screenshots of the scorecard or stats screens → vision extraction → `round_holes` columns for putts/fir/gir. Reconcile against the export's `holeStrokes`.
4. **Access layer:** a static dashboard (your usual GitHub Pages pattern, aggregates only) plus an optional local FastMCP server over `golf.db`.
5. **Automation (optional, your decision on ToS risk):** a weekly script that replicates `userLogin` → `getMyData`. Default instead: a manual download on a reminder.

## Archive schema (observed Dec 2025; same keys used by a June 2026 parser)
```
myData
  accountData {userId, userName, accountCreatedSource, registerTimestamp, birthYear, mobileNumber, email}   # PII -> drop
  activityData {roundCount, rounds[ {id, timestamp(ms), clubId{id}, score(to-par), strokes, holeStrokes[int x 9|18], stats{...25 keys} } ]}
  clubData {playedClubs[{clubId, name}], postedInClubs[...]}
  feedData {messageCount, messages[{messageId, content?}]}   # your posts: may hold free-text notes
  friendData {friendCount, friends[{userId,name}]}           # PII -> drop
  subscriptionData {status, paymentMethod, expiredTimestamp}
```

## Target tables
```sql
rounds(round_id TEXT PK, played_at_utc TIMESTAMP, played_date_local DATE,  -- convert ms epoch to America/New_York
       club_id TEXT, club_name TEXT, holes_played INT, strokes INT, to_par INT, total_par INT,  -- total_par = strokes - to_par
       is_complete BOOL, is_9 BOOL, fw_hit INT, fw_left INT, fw_right INT, fw_short INT, fw_long INT, fw_chances INT,
       gir INT, gir_left INT, gir_right INT, gir_short INT, gir_long INT, gir_no_chance INT, gir_chances INT,
       putts INT, eagles INT, birdies INT, pars INT, bogeys INT, dbl_plus INT, aces INT,
       source TEXT DEFAULT '18b_export', export_file TEXT, dq_flags TEXT)
round_holes(round_id, hole_no INT, strokes INT, par INT NULL, si INT NULL, putts INT NULL, fir TEXT NULL, gir BOOL NULL, source TEXT)
clubs(club_id PK, name, default_course, default_tee, rating REAL, slope INT)
club_holes(club_id, course, hole_no, par, si, yards_default_tee)
```

## Parsing rules and data-quality flags
- Upsert by `round_id`. Each export is a full snapshot, so re-running is idempotent. Keep all raw snapshots so you can detect edits and deletions.
- `holeStrokes` value 0 means the hole was not played. Set `holes_played = count(>0)`. Mark `is_complete` when holes_played is 9 or 18.
- Drop rounds with `strokes == 0` (abandoned rounds; 7 of 75 in the sample).
- Flag `sum(holeStrokes) != strokes` (8 of 75 in the sample). Flag partial rounds (19 of 75 in the sample).
- `strokeGain* == 100` is a sentinel meaning not available, so store NULL. Treat `puttHoleCount` as unreliable (it was 0 even when putts > 0). Stats are zero when not tracked, so use `fairwayHoleCount` / `girHoleCount` > 0 to tell 'not tracked' apart from 'zero'.
- Normalize 9-hole rounds (×2, or analyze them separately) before trend modeling. Differentials need rating/slope from `courses.yaml`.
- Validate with a Pydantic model and `extra='allow'`, and log any new keys so schema drift in future exports gets noticed.

## Web call sequence (reference only; not executed)
```
POST https://18birdies.com/usercentral/api/user/userLogin      {"account": "<email>", "password": "..."}  -> {token, user}
  (phone: POST /usercentral/api/user/sendVerificationCode {account, alpha2Code}; then userLogin {account, verificationCode, alpha2Code})
POST https://18birdies.com/usercentral/api/user/getMyData      {}   headers: {"Token": token, "content-type": "application/json"} -> {myData:{...}}
```

## Local MCP tool sketch
`import_archive(path)`, `list_rounds(since?, club?, complete_only=True)`, `get_round(round_id)`, `trends(window=10, metric='to_par'|'putts'|'gir_pct'|'fw_pct')`, `timeline(start?, end?)` (lesson and practice events from the notes area), `compare_periods(event_id, n_before=10, n_after=10)`.

## Privacy
The raw archive holds your email, phone, birth year and friends list. Never commit it or publish it to GitHub Pages; publish only derived aggregates. Course names plus dates also reveal your whereabouts, so consider a private repo, or publish only relative dates.

load_bearing_claims.claim: 18Birdies offers a self-serve web export at https://18birdies.com/download-account-data/ that, after web sign-in, immediately downloads 18Birdies_archive.json containing all of the user's rounds

The export's per-round fields are id, timestamp (ms), clubId, score (to par), strokes, holeStrokes (per-hole strokes for 9 or 18 holes), and round-level aggregate stats (scoring distribution, fairway/GIR hit and miss direction, total putts); it lacks per-hole par/putts/FIR/GIR, tee, rating/slope and shots

The archive's clubId UUID resolves to a public club page at 18birdies.com/golf-courses/club/<clubId>/<slug> listing per-hole par, stroke index, yardage and per-tee rating/slope

questions_for_user: Does your 18Birdies login use email + password or phone number + SMS code? (Only email + password allows any unattended automated download.)

Would you rather download the export by hand every few weeks (fully sanctioned), or have a weekly script replicate the website's login + getMyData calls (convenient, but a gray area under the ToS's 'automated means' clause)?
Do you track putts, fairways and GIR per hole in 18Birdies? If so, per-hole analysis needs the screenshot/vision path, since the export has only round-level totals.
Which courses and tees do you usually play? A one-time per-course mapping (par, stroke index, tee rating/slope) unlocks per-hole score-to-par and handicap differentials.
Do you post scores to GHIN (or have a GHIN number)? If so, GHIN could supply official rating, slope and differentials.

Will the dashboard be public on GitHub Pages? The raw export contains your email, phone, birth year and friends, and round dates plus courses reveal your location patterns, so plan to publish aggregates only or keep the repo private.

Where do your golf notes live (Apple Notes, a doc, 18Birdies' in-app hole/course Notes, 18Birdies feed posts)? In-app Notes did not appear in the sample export, though your own feed posts' text does (feedData.messages[].content).

verdicts.correction: The counts are right (7 with strokes==0, 19 with a 0 hole and strokes>0, 8 mismatches), but the reading and the rule are wrong. Of the 8 mismatches, 6 have holeStrokes all zero with strokes of 99 to 110 and a normal to-par (e.g. 100/+29). These are full rounds entered by total score only, which the app allows via 'Enter a Past Round' 'by total score' (https://help.18birdies.com/article/51-entering-a-past-round, Aug 10 2026). The proposed rule would give them holes_played=0 and drop them as incomplete. Treat strokes>0 with sum(holeStrokes)==0 as a total-only round: holes = len(holeStrokes), total_par = strokes - score. Keep it for score trends and exclude it from per-hole analysis. For real partial rounds (e.g. 4 holes, 21 strokes, +5), score is relative to the par of the holes played only.

verification.missed_options:
1) OpenGolfAPI for course enrichment. This avoids scraping 18Birdies club pages, which the ToS forbids. It is keyless REST plus an MCP server, with data under ODbL 1.0 (attribution required) and MIT-licensed code at https://github.com/opengolfapi/mcp-server (created Apr 2026, pushed Aug 2026). I tested it: GET https://api.opengolfapi.org/api/v1/courses/search?q=Skaneateles returned the course. /courses/{id}/holes returned per-hole par, handicap_index and yardage by tee. /courses/{id}/tees returned rating, slope, par and yardage per tee and gender. Caveats: (a) there is no shared ID with the 18Birdies clubId, so the join has to be a fuzzy match on name and location from playedClubs, plus a one-time manual check; (b) its ratings differ from 18Birdies' page for the same course (Black men 71.2/132 at OpenGolfAPI vs 72.2/136 at 18Birdies), so check the tees you actually play against the USGA Course Rating database (ncrdb.usga.org; not fetched here) before computing differentials. Sources: https://opengolfapi.org/ and https://api.opengolfapi.org/openapi.json.

2) 18Birdies' in-app Practice Log and hole Notes bear directly on the lesson/practice timeline. Practice mode records each session's date, duration, type (putting, short game, full swing) and free-text notes, with a History > Timeline view (https://help.18birdies.com/article/524-practice-overview, Aug 10 2026; https://help.18birdies.com/article/525-practice-history). Hole Notes persist per hole across rounds (https://help.18birdies.com/article/543-using-notes). Neither shows up in the sample export's sections, so if Shane logs practice or notes in 18Birdies he would likely need screenshots plus vision to get them out. Unconfirmed: whether the export adds a practice section for users who actually log practice; the sample user may never have used it.

3) Total-score-only rounds. 'Enter a Past Round' can record a total score only (https://help.18birdies.com/article/51-entering-a-past-round). In the sample, 6 full rounds of this kind (holeStrokes all zero, strokes around 100) would be wrongly treated as incomplete by the proposed parser. Past rounds Shane never logged can also be backfilled in-app so the export captures them.

4) The official partnership inquiry form (https://help.18birdies.com/article/771-how-do-i-request-a-partnership, June 19 2026) is the sanctioned place to ask for written authorization to script the export, which would resolve the ToS 'expressly authorized in writing' issue for option 2.

5) A formal data request by email to support@18birdies.com. The privacy policy (https://18birdies.com/legal/privacy-policy/, last updated Jan 29 2021) grants portability only to EU residents, plus a narrow California disclosure right. A US (Massachusetts) user has no guaranteed right, and it is unconfirmed whether a manual request would return more than the self-serve export (e.g. per-hole putts, FIR or GIR).

6) Prior art for the screenshot path: bjornj12/golf-coach (in the official MCP registry, v0.7.0, updated Jul 2026) ingests Golf GameBook round screenshots with a 'gamebook-screenshot-analysis' skill. ChristianJBNB/18Birdies-Scores (Feb to Mar 2026) OCRs 18Birdies scorecard screenshots with OpenCV and Tesseract, using fixed crop ratios (fragile; a vision LLM is the better choice). Use both as design references only; do not install either.

7) The in-app End of Year Summary (https://help.18birdies.com/article/689-end-of-year-summary) gives yearly averages, fairways, GIR, putts and lowest/highest handicap. It is a cheap yearly cross-check for the parsed totals, available only in the app.
verification.corrected_bottom_line:
The researcher's core conclusion holds. There is no 18Birdies API and no official or community MCP with live access. The only supported way to get your data is the self-serve export at https://18birdies.com/download-account-data/: sign in, and it immediately downloads 18Birdies_archive.json. I confirmed this from the site's own JS and from help article 780 (July 2, 2026). The file gives, for every round, the date, club UUID, gross score, score to par and per-hole strokes, plus round-level fairway, GIR and putt totals. It has no per-hole putts, fairways or GIR, no tee, no notes and no practice data. So the realistic "MCP" is your own local server over a store built from that export. Feasibility ratings for options 1, 2 and 4 to 10 stand. For option 3, the scraping risk is avoidable by using the keyless OpenGolfAPI. Corrections and caveats:

1. **Login method.** The web export form accepts only email+password or phone+SMS code; this comes from the JS, not from the cited help article, which says there is no web login portal. Help article 786 shows the app also allows Apple and Google sign-in. If your account uses only one of those, connect an email or phone in the app first.
2. **Parser rule.** The proposed rule would drop valid rounds. Rounds with strokes > 0 but all-zero holeStrokes are full rounds entered by total score only (6 of the 8 mismatches in the sample). Keep them for score trends and exclude them from per-hole analysis.
3. **Course data.** For per-hole par, stroke index and rating/slope, use OpenGolfAPI (keyless, ODbL) rather than scraping 18Birdies club pages. Match courses by name, and check the rating/slope of the tees you play against USGA, because the two sources disagree.
4. **Timeline and in-app notes.** If you use 18Birdies' Practice Log or hole Notes, they do not appear in the sample export's sections, so they would need screenshots and vision too. Otherwise your own notes stay the source for the timeline.
5. **Strava.** Manual sharing of any single past round is possible, but Strava's June 2026 policy bans AI use of API data and requires a subscription, so it stays not recommended.
6. **Written authorization.** Automating the export (login, then getMyData) works technically but conflicts with the ToS unless you get written permission. Ask for it through the partnership form in help article 771, not through general support email.

Recommended: download the export by hand, parse it with Pydantic into SQLite, enrich courses from OpenGolfAPI plus a small hand-checked tee map, use screenshots and vision only for per-hole putts, fairways, GIR and practice/notes, and run a local FastMCP server over the store.

research.area: Indirect data paths: GHIN/WHS score posting, course-rating data sources, Apple Health, and third-party golf aggregators
research.summary: The biggest find sits just outside this area: 18Birdies has an official web page, "Download Your Account Data" (https://18birdies.com/download-account-data/). You sign in with email and password, or phone plus an SMS code. The page then POSTs to /usercentral/api/user/getMyData and saves your whole history as 18Birdies_archive.json. The page says the archive includes "activities, photos, posts, rounds and more". I read the site's JS on 2026-09-25 to confirm this. Two independent GitHub parsers, from 2025 and June 2026, show what each round holds: date (epoch ms), club id and name, gross strokes, score to par, a holeStrokes[] array with per-hole strokes, and round-level stats. The stats cover fairways (L/M/R/short/long), GIR by miss direction, putts, the scoring distribution, and a strokes-gained field that is premium-gated. So the complete history is recoverable today with no MCP, no screenshots and no ToS risk. What the archive seems to lack is tee name, course rating/slope and per-hole par; I have not confirmed that. Everything indirect ranks well below it. 18Birdies does not post to GHIN or any other WHS network (their help page, updated 2026-07-24, says no sync and no timeline). GHIN therefore holds only the rounds Shane posted there himself, with hole-by-hole detail and putts/FIR/GIR only if he entered them in GHIN. GHIN's unofficial golfer API (api2.ghin.com: golfer_login.json, then /golfers/{ghin}/scores.json and handicap_history.json) still worked in several 2026 projects. It is the only source of official differentials, PCC and Handicap Index history, but the GHIN ToS bans automated access and someone reported a Cloudflare captcha in Dec 2025. For course rating/slope/par, the practical choices are: a small hand-kept course table checked against USGA NCRDB, GolfCourseAPI (free, 35 requests/day, per-tee CR/slope plus per-hole par/yardage/handicap), GHIN course details if he uses GHIN, or OpenGolfAPI (ODbL, free, but it doesn't say where its ratings come from). Apple Health adds almost nothing: 18Birdies declares no health data, and Watch golf workouts carry no strokes. None of TheGrint, Garmin Golf, Arccos or Golfshot imports from 18Birdies.

options.name: 1. 18Birdies official account-data archive (18Birdies_archive.json) — found here, but it is really a direct path

The page's JS (DownloadAccountData.41460882.js, read 2026-09-25) POSTs {} to https://18birdies.com/usercentral/api/user/getMyData with a 'Token' header from /usercentral/api/user/userLogin. It checks that the response has a myData key and saves the JSON straight away as 18Birdies_archive.json, with no email wait. The error text also mentions an in-app path ('try again via 18Birdies Settings'). Parse myData.activityData.rounds[] and join to myData.clubData.playedClubs[] on clubId.id. To refresh, re-download before each analysis run (manual), or later script the same two calls as a gray-area reuse of the site's own endpoints with his own account.

options.name: 2. GHIN via the unofficial golfer API (api2.ghin.com) — only covers rounds Shane posted to GHIN
options.how_it_works: This is the same flow the GHIN.com web app uses. POST https://api2.ghin.com/api/v1/golfer_login.json with {user:{email_or_ghin, password, remember_me}, token:<pre-auth>}. The current GHIN.com bundle sends token={source:'GHINcom', datetime}; libraries use a Firebase Installations token for project ghin-mobile-app, and some use a placeholder string. The call returns golfer_user.golfer_user_token, a JWT that lasts about 12h. Then GET /api/v1/golfers/{ghin}/scores.json (optional only_with_stats=true, from/to_date_played, limit/offset) and /golfers/{ghin}/handicap_history.json?date_begin&date_end, both with Authorization: Bearer. Clients: npm @spicygolf/ghin v0.20.0 (2026-09-04, maintained fork) or n8io/ghin 0.7.0 (2025-07). There is no PyPI package; Python examples use plain requests (quantified-self-app, golf-reports).
options.data_obtained: Per score: id, played_at, posted_at, course_id, course_name, facility_name, number_of_holes, course_rating, slope_rating, front9/back9 rating and slope, adjusted_gross_score, front9/back9_adjusted, differential, unadjusted_differential, net_score_differential, pcc, course_handicap, handicap_index at the time, score_type (H/A/T=competition/C=combined 9+9/E/P), status (Validated/UnderReview/Temporary), used (counts in the current index), exceptional, adjustments. hole_details[] only for hole-by-hole posts: hole_number, par, stroke_allocation, raw_score, adjusted_gross_score, putts, fairway_hit, gir_flag, drive_accuracy, approach_shot_accuracy, x_hole. statistics block only if stats were entered: putts_total, gir_percent, fairway_hits_percent, miss-direction percents, par3/4/5 averages, 1/2/3-putt percents, up_and_downs_total. Plus Handicap Index revision history. Tee name is not in the known schemas (unconfirmed).
options.effort: Low: about 2-3 hours with requests plus pandas. Store credentials in the Keychain and re-login each run.
options.risks: The GHIN ToS prohibit 'any other automatic or unauthorized means of accessing, logging-in' (the USGA ToS page blocks fetches; the quote comes from a search snippet). Personal read-only use of his own data is low risk in practice but not sanctioned. Dec 2025 issue: 'GHIN login now has a Cloudflare Captcha'. Against that, projects from Mar-Sep 2026 still log in programmatically, and the GHIN.com JS bundle fetched 2026-09-25 contains no captcha/turnstile strings. Treat it as fragile. The fallback is pasting the Bearer JWT from DevTools every 12h, which is what golf-reports documents. Response schemas drift: NaN stats and the new 'Temporary' status broke parsers in Apr 2026. The fork mentions a per-account rate limit. GHIN needs a paid club membership, e.g. Mass Golf Members Now! at about $60/yr (from a search snippet). The recovered history equals whatever he posted; 18Birdies never auto-posts.

research.design_notes:
## Ranking (history recovered × reliability)

| Rank | Source | History recovered | Reliability / risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **18Birdies account-data archive** (web, official) | ALL 18Birdies rounds: per-hole strokes, round stats | Official export; schema undocumented |
| 2 | Course table (NCRDB manual + GolfCourseAPI autofill) | Supplies CR/slope/par/SI that the archive lacks | Stable, cheap |
| 3 | GHIN unofficial API | Only rounds he posted; adds official differentials, PCC, index history | ToS gray, captcha risk, schema drift |
| 4 | GHIN manual copy | Same as 3 | Tedious |
| 5 | Apple Health | Workout dates at best | Near-zero value |
| 6 | Aggregators | None | Not possible |

**Implication for the overall plan:** the screenshot/vision path becomes a fallback for new rounds between archive downloads, or an optional quick-add. It is not needed to recover history. Another agent should verify the archive against Shane's real account (field list, whether per-hole putts/FIR exist, 9-hole handling).

## Ingest pipeline (Python, fits his existing stack)
```
raw/18birdies/{YYYY-MM-DD}_archive.json   # immutable snapshots (gitignored, private)
raw/ghin/{date}_scores.json, _handicap_history.json   # optional
ref/courses.yaml                           # hand-verified CR/slope/par/SI per tee
build/golf.duckdb (or sqlite)              # normalized tables below
site/  -> static HTML/SVG dashboard (only derived, non-PII data)
```

### Tables
- `round(round_id PK, source ENUM('18b','ghin','screenshot'), source_id, date_local, course_key, tee_key NULL, holes_played, gross, to_par, putts, fir_hit, fir_chances, gir, gir_chances, fw_miss_l, fw_miss_r, gir_miss_l/r/s/long, birdies, pars, bogeys, dbl_plus, ghin_score_id NULL, ghin_differential NULL, ghin_pcc NULL, ghin_used NULL)`
- `hole(round_id, hole_no, strokes, par NULL, si NULL, putts NULL, fir NULL, gir NULL)`: from holeStrokes[] or GHIN hole_details
- `course(course_key, name_18b, club_id_18b, ghin_course_id NULL, gca_id NULL)`; `tee(tee_key, course_key, name, gender, cr18, slope18, bogey18 NULL, cr_f9, slope_f9, cr_b9, slope_b9, par18, effective_from)`; `tee_hole(tee_key, hole_no, par, si, yards)`
- `index_history(date, handicap_index, source)`: GHIN revisions, or recomputed

### 18Birdies archive parse (confirmed paths)
`data['myData']['activityData']['rounds'][*]`: `timestamp` (ms, convert to America/New_York date), `clubId.id`, `strokes`, `score`, `holeStrokes[]`, `stats.{putts, puttHoleCount, fairwayMiddles, fairwayLefts, fairwayRights, fairwayShorts, fairwayLongs, fairwayHoleCount, gir, girLefts, girRights, girShorts, girLongs, girNoChances, girHoleCount, eagles, birdies, pars, bogeys, doubleBogeyOrWorse, aces, doubleEagleOrBetter, strokeGainOverall, strokeGainTeeToGreen}`. Join `data['myData']['clubData']['playedClubs'][*]` on `id`→`name`. holes_played = count of non-zero holeStrokes. Do NOT infer par as strokes−|score|, which is wrong under par. Use par = strokes − score.

### GHIN parse (if used)
`GET /api/v1/golfers/{ghin}/scores.json?limit=100&offset=…&from_date_played=…` → `scores[*]`; `GET /api/v1/golfers/{ghin}/handicap_history.json?date_begin=…&date_end=…`. Validate with lenient Pydantic models: allow NaN or missing, and status ∈ {Validated, UnderReview, Temporary}.

### GHIN ↔ 18Birdies match
Candidate pairs: same local date. Score = |gross_18b − AGS_ghin| (AGS ≤ gross because of the net-double-bogey cap) + course-name fuzzy distance (rapidfuzz token_set_ratio). Accept if AGS ≤ gross ≤ AGS+8 and name ratio ≥ 70. Else leave unmatched. Handle doubles by score_day_order.

### Differential math (WHS; compute yourself when GHIN is absent)
- Course Handicap = round(HI × Slope/113 + (CR − Par)).
- Per-hole max for AGS = Net Double Bogey = par + 2 + strokes received on that hole, where strokes received come from the Course Handicap distributed by stroke index (SI). With no index yet, the cap is par + 5.
- Score Differential = (113 / Slope) × (AGS − CR − PCC). Assume PCC = 0 unless GHIN supplies it. Round to 1 decimal.
- 9-hole rounds: since 2024 WHS combines the 9-hole differential with an expected-score differential based on the player's index. Easiest is to flag 9-hole rounds and exclude them from a self-computed index, or use GHIN's value when available.
- Index = mean of the lowest 8 of the most recent 20 differentials (fewer-round table for <20) × 1.0. Label it "unofficial".

### course.yaml example
```yaml
- course_key: "stow-acres-north"
  names_18b: ["Stow Acres Country Club - North"]
  tees:
    - {name: White, gender: M, cr18: 70.1, slope18: 125, par18: 72, cr_f9: 35.0, slope_f9: 124, cr_b9: 35.1, slope_b9: 126,
       effective_from: 2024-01-01, source: NCRDB,
       holes: [{no: 1, par: 4, si: 7, yds: 380}, ...]}
```
(Values are illustrative only. Fill them from NCRDB or the scorecard; GolfCourseAPI `GET /v1/courses/{id}` can auto-fill `holes` with par/yardage/handicap.)

### Tee inference
The archive seems to lack tee info. Default to the tee Shane marks as usual per course in course.yaml, with a per-round override column, or take the tee from a GHIN match.

### Credentials
18Birdies and GHIN passwords/tokens go in the macOS Keychain (`security add-generic-password`) via the Python `keyring` package, never in the repo or GitHub Actions secrets for a public repo. The archive and GHIN pulls should run locally, not in CI. Publish only aggregated or derived data to GitHub Pages.

The GHIN.com pre-auth token is not the plain {source:'GHINcom', datetime}: the bundle RSA-encrypts that JSON with a public key (function MVe → DHe uses forge pki.publicKeyFromPem). verdicts.claim: GHIN scores.json returns course_name, course_rating, slope_rating, adjusted_gross_score, differential, pcc, score_type, status, used and hole_details (par, stroke_allocation, raw_score, putts, fairway_hit, gir_flag); tee name is not in the known schemas.
verdicts.evidence: The boorad/ghin score model (https://github.com/boorad/ghin/blob/main/src/client/ghin/models/scores/score.ts) includes course_name, facility_name, course_rating, slope_rating, front9/back9 rating and slope, adjusted_gross_score, differential, unadjusted_differential, net_score_differential, pcc, course_handicap, handicap_index, score_type, status (Validated/UnderReview/Temporary), used, exceptional, hole_details and statistics. n8io hole-detail.ts and statistics.ts include raw_score, stroke_allocation, gir_flag, fairway_hit, drive_accuracy, approach_shot_accuracy, x_hole, putts_total and up_and_downs_total. The public SwaggerHub spec (https://api.swaggerhub.com/apis/GHIN/GHIN2020AllSandbox/1.0) lists GET /golfers/{golfer_id}/scores (only_with_stats) and /golfers/{id}/handicap_history (date_begin, date_end, rev_count, include_hidden), and says 'a new token needs to be generated every 24h'.
verdicts.correction: The tee-name statement is refuted. The SwaggerHub scores response schema includes tee_name, tee_set_id, tee_set_side, front9_tee_name and back9_tee_name. The zod models omit them because zod strips unknown keys. A GHIN match can therefore supply the tee for matched rounds.

The other formulas match standard WHS/USGA rules. I did not re-fetch primary text for each.

verification.missed_options:
1. 18Birdies → Strava auto-sync (new June 16, 2026; free for all 18Birdies users). Setup: Me → … → Connected Apps & Devices → Strava. Each round shared to Strava carries course name and location, gross score, birdies/pars/bogeys, round duration, and an 'End-of-round summary graphic, including your scorecard and key round statistics'. Auto-sync only covers rounds completed after connecting whose visibility was 'Everyone' before completion. Older rounds can be shared one at a time from Round Summary → Share → Strava. Sources: https://help.18birdies.com/article/762-strava-integration (updated 2026-06-16) and https://18birdies.com/clubhouse/company-news/strava-18birdies-share-golf-rounds.

1a. Strava official MCP connector (https://mcp.strava.com/mcp, listed in the Anthropic MCP registry; launched June 1, 2026). It is read-only, subscribers only (trials excluded), and works in Claude.ai, Cowork and Claude Code. Sources: https://support.strava.com/en-us/articles/15401531-what-is-the-strava-mcp-connector and https://press.strava.com/articles/strava-launches-mcp-connector. This is the only sanctioned MCP path to 18Birdies round summaries, and it is the closest thing to Shane's 'tap 18Birdies through MCP' idea. It needs a Strava subscription, about $11.99/mo or $79.99/yr (per https://appsforstrava.com/blog/strava-developer-program-changes-2026). Unverified: whether list_activities returns the activity description text or the scorecard graphic, so per-hole data may not come through.

1b. Strava API custom pipeline: be careful. Strava API Policy (2026) §5.3 (https://www.strava.com/legal/api_policy, effective June 1, 2026) bans using Strava Data 'in connection with the ... operation of any AI Application', explicitly including 'ingestion into a context window'. Only the Strava MCP is exempt. So sending Strava-sourced scorecard images to Claude vision through his own API app would violate the policy. Since June 2026, Standard-tier API apps also require an active Strava subscription. Plain non-AI parsing of his own activities is not banned by §5.3, but I have not reviewed the rest of the policy (e.g. §5.4).

2. In-app 'Share Scorecard' from Round Summary (email or share sheet), documented at https://help.18birdies.com/article/249-can-i-email-a-scorecard-to-myself. This is an official per-round image source for the vision path. It may show per-hole par and tees, which the archive lacks (unverified; the article does not describe the image).

3. A real archive sample is public: https://github.com/ericlu28/18birdies-wrapped (committed 2025-12-18). It confirms the exact schema, so a parser can be built and tested before Shane downloads his own. It contains that person's PII (email, phone, birth year), so use it for schema reference only. Do not copy it or the repo's code (no license checked).

4. 18Birdies 'My Performance' (Aug 2026; https://18birdies.com/clubhouse/play/my-performance) gives in-app per-course history and stats (premium adds hole-by-hole and an eclectic scorecard). There is no export, but it is a possible screenshot source.

5. Data-quality work the researcher did not plan for, taken from the real schema:
- The join key is playedClubs.clubId.
- clubId is facility-level, not course-level.
- 9-hole rounds come as either 9-length or zero-padded 18-length arrays.
- Empty rounds (strokes − score = 0) and sum(holeStrokes) ≠ strokes mismatches both occur.
- strokeGain fields are always 100 for non-premium accounts.
- The archive includes email, phone, birth year, friends and payment-method status, so it must stay local.
verification.corrected_bottom_line:
The researcher's main finding holds up and is stronger than stated. 18Birdies has an official download page (https://18birdies.com/download-account-data/) that returns the full history as 18Birdies_archive.json after an email+password or phone+SMS login. I confirmed this from the site JS and the structure of a real archive. There is no Apple/Google sign-in to worry about.

What each round in the archive contains:
- id, timestamp (epoch ms), clubId.id, strokes, score to par, and holeStrokes.
- Aggregate stats: fairway/GIR miss counts, putts, and the scoring distribution. Strokes-gained is a sentinel value of 100.
- Nothing else: no tee, rating/slope, per-hole par, per-hole putts/FIR/GIR or course-within-facility. This is now confirmed rather than inferred.
- Join course names on playedClubs[].clubId, not id.
- The file holds sensitive PII (email, phone, birth year, friends, payment status), so keep it local.

Corrections to the other findings:
- **Aggregators and MCP:** The researcher missed that 18Birdies has auto-shared rounds to Strava since June 2026 (course, gross, birdies/pars/bogeys, duration, a scorecard graphic). Strava's official, read-only MCP connector in the Anthropic registry can read those activities for Strava subscribers. That makes it the only sanctioned MCP path to his 18Birdies data. It gives totals for new rounds, not history, and per-hole detail is unverified. Strava's 2026 API Policy forbids feeding Strava API data into any AI outside that MCP.
- **GHIN:** The unofficial API is still plausible but only evidenced through April 2026. Today api2.ghin.com is not behind Cloudflare. GHIN score records do include tee_name, tee_set_side and front/back tee names, contrary to the researcher. It covers only rounds Shane posted and is against GHIN's ToS.
- **GolfCourseAPI:** It works today (35 requests/day free). Real responses probably also include optional bogey and front/back-nine ratings. Its terms forbid publishing the data.
- Apple Health (near-zero value) and the golf aggregators (no import from 18Birdies) stand as rated.

Recommended plan:
1. Archive download for history.
2. A hand-checked course/tee table (NCRDB and scorecard, with GolfCourseAPI to autofill) for par/SI/CR/slope.
3. For new rounds, either re-download the archive, or use the Strava MCP if he already pays for Strava, or use a Claude-vision parse of his own 18Birdies 'Share Scorecard' screenshot. Do not use Strava API images for that.
4. GHIN only if he posts there and accepts the ToS gray area.

Ask Shane whether he has a Strava subscription and whether he posts to GHIN.

research.area: Extracting round data from 18Birdies screenshots with Claude vision
research.summary:
Pulling rounds out of 18Birdies screenshots with Claude vision is practical and cheap. 18Birdies has no CSV export. Its public help pages show 3–4 screens that together hold everything needed. (1) The Round Summary has all 18 hole scores with birdie/bogey symbols, the front and back totals, Gross/Net, To Par, course par, tee yardage, date and duration. It does not show par or putts per hole. (2) The Full Scorecard has a "Scores / Stats" toggle. It shows par, stroke index (labelled "Handicap"), putts, fairway (FH), GIR, chips, sand shots and penalties per hole, but in portrait it needs sideways swipes. (3) The More Stats → Benchmarks table has this round's totals, which we can use as a checksum.

Claude vision accepts only JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP (no HEIC), but iOS already saves screenshots as PNG. Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 read an iPhone screenshot at almost full resolution, about 3,956 input tokens each (calculated with Anthropic's own resize code). A round of 4–8 screenshots costs about $0.17–0.37 on claude-opus-5, $0.07–0.15 on claude-sonnet-5, and half that through the Batch API.

The main design limit is in structured outputs. They reject min/max constraints on numbers and allow at most 16 fields that can be "either value or empty" (nullable). So the schema I propose makes every field required and marks unknowns with -1 or enum values like "not_visible". It records per-field confidence as a short list of uncertain fields per hole rather than wrapping every value.

A set of plain-code checks then catches most misreads, because the screens repeat the same numbers several ways: hole sums vs the printed Out/In/Gross, symbol vs strokes minus par, putts and fairways vs the Benchmarks totals, stroke dots vs Gross minus Net, and GIR vs strokes minus putts. Any flagged cell goes to a human review screen, and every correction is saved so it becomes test data. Apple's on-device text recognition (ocrmac, or the newer table reader on macOS 26) is a free check on the digits but cannot read the circle/square symbols. The Batch API fits a backfill of old rounds.

Two new leads: 18Birdies has a "Download Your Account Data" page (you log in yourself; it says the archive includes rounds, format unknown) that could make a screenshot backfill unnecessary. The full-scorecard layout, especially landscape mode, still needs checking against Shane's own screenshots.

options.name: A. Claude vision + structured outputs, one request per round (primary path)
options.how_it_works: Shane saves 3–4 standard screenshots per round (Round Summary, Full Scorecard in both Scores and Stats views, and More Stats → Benchmarks). A local Python script groups them by round and labels each 'Image N:'. It sends all of a round's screenshots in one request to client.messages.parse() on claude-opus-5 with adaptive thinking and a Pydantic schema (claude-sonnet-5 is the cheaper option). The schema has no nullable fields; unknowns use -1 or enum sentinels. The model merges overlapping swipes itself and lists which image each hole came from. Plain-code checks and a review step follow (see design_notes). Don't stitch the images into one tall picture: a 1206x6000 strip gets shrunk to 518x2576 (43%), and small digits become hard to read.
options.data_obtained: Round: player, course name and subname, date (raw text and ISO), tee name, tee total yards, course par, rating/slope (if shown), duration, holes played, handicap before/after, weather. Per hole: number, par (plus the second value of a men's/women's pair), yardage, stroke index, gross strokes, score symbol (eagle/birdie/par/bogey/double/max), net strokes, stroke dots received, putts, fairway (hit/left/right/short/long/miss/n.a.), GIR (hit/miss plus miss direction if shown), chips, greenside sand shots, penalties, confidence, uncertain fields, inferred fields, source images. Printed totals: Out, In, Gross, Net, To Par, total putts, fairways hit, GIR, penalties, pars or better, 3-putt holes, and the GIR%, FH%, putts-per-hole, up-and-down and sand-save text. Up-and-down and sand saves are computed in code, not read.
options.effort: About 2–3 days for extraction, checks and SQLite storage. Another 1–2 days for a local review page. Plus about half a day building a 10-round ground-truth set from Shane's own screenshots.
options.risks: Misreading small glyphs (1/7, 3/8, single vs double square) and which player's row is which. 18Birdies redesigns its screens often: the scorecard UI changed in 2023 and 2024 and landscape mode arrived in July 2024, so the prompt will need upkeep. Screenshots go to the Anthropic API, but they only hold golf data; nothing is signed in and no credentials are involved. The API key comes from the environment or an `ant auth login` profile. There is a small chance the schema hits the API's 'Schema is too complex' error; test once. The 18Birdies Terms of Service don't matter here because Shane is only screenshotting his own screen.

evidence.claim: Only JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP are supported. Max 8000x8000 px; 10 MB base64 per image; 600 images per request (1M-context models); above 20 images every image must be 2000 px or smaller; the request limit is 32 MB.

Visual tokens = ceil(w/28) x ceil(h/28). Claude 4.7 and later models are in the high-resolution tier (2576 px long edge, 4784 visual tokens). Anthropic publishes a reference implementation of the resize.

Structured outputs work with images and batches. They don't support minimum/maximum or maxItems. Limits: 24 optional parameters and 16 union-typed parameters. The Python SDK strips unsupported constraints and checks them on the client. Enum capitalization is not guaranteed.

The 18Birdies scorecard legend, last updated Aug 10, 2026: '4/5' = men's/women's par or hole handicap; double circle = eagle; circle = birdie; plain = par; square = bogey; double square = double bogey; red starburst = Max; black/red dots = strokes received/given; orange asterisk = score changed by another player.

Round Summary: date, course, Course Par, Tee + yards, Duration, To Par, Gross/Net, a condensed 2x9 score grid with front/back totals, 'View Full Scorecard', and the More Stats → Benchmarks and Hole Insights screens (article updated Apr 10, 2025; the article's example screenshot shows a Nov 2023 round).
Classic Score Entry records score, putts, fairway, GIR, penalties, chips and sand shots per hole (updated Aug 12, 2026).

options.name: B. Cheaper model mix: claude-sonnet-5 first, escalate to claude-opus-5 only when checks fail
options.how_it_works: Same pipeline as A, but the first pass runs on claude-sonnet-5, which also reads images at full high resolution and costs $2/$10 per million tokens. If any hard check fails, or more than N cells are flagged, the same request is rerun on claude-opus-5. Optionally run two passes and send any cell where they disagree to review.
options.data_obtained: Same as A.
options.effort: About 0.5 day on top of A: a model switch plus a loop that measures accuracy against the ground-truth set.
options.risks: Sonnet may misread symbols more often. Measure against Shane's hand-checked rounds before making it the default. The cache is per model, which hardly matters at this volume.

evidence.claim: Sonnet 5 has high-resolution vision (2576 px) (from the claude-api skill's cached model notes); the vision doc puts every model from 'Claude 4.7 and later' in the high-resolution tier.

options.name: C. On-device Apple Vision OCR as a free check on the digits
options.how_it_works: Run ocrmac (pip; MIT license; v1.0.1 from Jan 2026; wraps pyobjc's VNRecognizeTextRequest; can also use the LiveText engine) on each screenshot. It returns text, confidence and a normalized box with the origin at the lower left. Group tokens into rows by y, then check that each Claude-extracted row of 9 scores, and the Out/In/Gross/Net/To Par/putts totals, appear in that order in the OCR output. On macOS 26 (Shane is on 26.5.1) the Swift-only RecognizeDocumentsRequest returns real table cells with row and column indices. That needs a small Swift command-line tool we write ourselves; pyobjc can't call Swift-only APIs (not verified).
options.data_obtained: Digit and text tokens with positions and confidence. It cannot read the circle/square symbols, the check/X icons or the stroke dots.
options.effort: About 1 day for ocrmac row matching; about 1–2 more days if we build the Swift table reader.
options.risks: Nothing leaves the Mac (fully local). Matching rows by position gets fragile on dark themes and in landscape. LiveText reports every confidence as 1. Avoid the unvetted third-party Swift tools that appear in search results and write our own instead.

evidence.claim: ocrmac wraps Apple's Vision framework and can use the 'vision' or 'livetext' engine; the latest release is v.1.0.1 (2026-01-08), MIT license.
Vision boundingBox is 'normalize[d]... with the origin at the lower-left corner of the image'.
The WWDC25 RecognizeDocumentsRequest detects tables, with cells grouped into rows and columns.

options.name: D. Message Batches API for backfilling old rounds
options.how_it_works: Build one batch request per round, keyed by a round id. Set output_config.format to transform_schema(TypeAdapter(ExtractedRound).json_schema()) and poll until the batch ends. Match results by that id, never by order, then validate each with ExtractedRound.model_validate_json and run the same checks and review queue. Leave out the server-side refusal fallback, which batches reject.
options.data_obtained: Same as A.
options.effort: About 0.5 day on top of A.
options.risks: Results can take up to 24 hours (usually under 1 hour) and are kept for 29 days. Images inside a batch count toward its 256 MB limit, so re-encode or shrink the PNGs.

evidence.claim: 50% off all usage. Up to 100,000 requests or 256 MB per batch. Most batches finish within 1 hour; a batch expires after 24 hours; results stay available for 29 days. Vision is supported, and the batch and caching discounts stack.
Structured outputs work with batch processing at the 50% discount.

options.name: E. Sorting camera-roll screenshots into rounds (for backfill)
options.how_it_works: First, skip exact duplicate files by hash and near-duplicates by image similarity. Then read the header text (date and course name) with free local OCR, or ask claude-haiku-4-5 about each image; Haiku uses the standard tier, about 1,456 tokens and $0.0015 per screenshot. It returns the screen type (round_summary, full_scorecard_scores/_stats, benchmarks, rounds_list, gps_hole, other) plus date and course. Group screenshots into rounds using those fields and the capture time, then send each group to path A or D. A 'Rounds Played' list screenshot can also give date, course and total score for many rounds at once, as a quick first pass (what each list row shows is not confirmed).
options.data_obtained: Screen type, date, course and gross score per screenshot; round groupings.
options.effort: About 1 day.
options.risks: Grouping mistakes when two rounds share a course. Needs review of the groupings.

evidence.claim: Standard-tier models (e.g., Haiku 4.5) cap images at 1568 px and 1568 tokens; a screenshot shrinks to about 723x1568.
Round History can be sorted and filtered by 18/9 holes, date, score, course and friends (updated Sep 11, 2026).

research.design_notes:
## 1. What the 18Birdies screens look like (checked Sep 2026)

App version 16.40.0 was released 2026-09-22 (iTunes lookup, id 892700751). The App Store and Play Store screenshots are marketing images. Only one Play image shows real round data: a summary grid "Monarch Bay … Gross/Net 102/77". The layouts below come from 18Birdies help-center images and are the most reliable source.

| Screen | How to reach it | What it shows | Full 18 on one screenshot? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Round Summary** | Me → Rounds Played → round (or straight after confirming a round) | `11/12/23` date plus weather and wind; course name and "(subname)"; `Course Par: 71  Tee: White 5516 yds  Duration: 4h 49m`; a dark card with `To Par +22` and `Gross/Net 93/78`; a condensed grid, row 1 = holes 1–9 with the front total (48) at the right, row 2 = holes 10–18 with the back total (45); hole numbers small above each score; each score wrapped in its symbol; "View Full Scorecard >"; a More Stats strip (Pars or Better 5, GIR 5.6%, FH 30.8%, Putts per Hole 1.6); "What to Work On"; buttons for trash, Share Scorecard, Exit. Further down: handicap change (e.g., 20.1 → 19.8) and a "Round Performance" section (Targets, Fairways Hit fan chart with Hit / Miss Left / Miss Right %, Greens Hit %). | **Yes for scores only.** Par, putts, FH and GIR per hole are **not** shown. |
| **Full Scorecard, Scores view** | "View Full Scorecard" (or the Scorecard tab during a round) | Header (date, course, tee, Gross/Net, stat strip). A **Scores / Stats** toggle. A grid with holes as columns plus Out/In/Tot, rows for Hole, Par/Handicap (stroke index; `4/5` = a men's/women's pair) and each player's Gross and Net. Stroke dots are drawn on holes. Notes markers appear here. | **No** in portrait: about 6 holes visible, swipe sideways (per a 2023 help GIF, low resolution). **Landscape mode** since July 2024 gives "a wider view"; how many holes it shows is **unconfirmed**. |
| **Full Scorecard, Stats view** | Toggle "Stats" | For one selected player, rows per hole: Score, Fairway Hit, Green in Regulation, Putts, Chip Shots, and below those (not seen) likely Greenside Sand Shots and Penalties. Entry icons are Fairway L/✓/R and GIR ✓/✗. | Same as the Scores view. |
| **Benchmarks** | Round Summary → More Stats → Benchmarks | Rows: GROSS, NET, FRONT 9, BACK 9, PAR OR BETTER, FAIRWAYS HIT, GREENS IN REGULATION, PUTTS PER HOLE, TOTAL PUTTS, HOLES WITH 3+ PUTTS, UP & DOWN, SAND SAVES, PENALTIES. Columns: THIS ROUND, a personal average, COURSE AVG, YOUR RANK (percentile). Tabs: Stats / Benchmarks / Hole Insights. | Yes, one screen: **the best checksum for putts, FH, GIR and penalties.** |
| Hole entry (GPS) | During a round | Header `1 · Mid Green 372 Yds · Par 4 · White 372 · Handicap 3`. Score keypad 1–9 with symbols plus "Others". Putts 0/1/2/3/≥4. FH ✓/✗ (a miss adds Left/Short/Right). GIR ✓/✗ (a miss adds Left/Long/Right/Short/No chance). Chips, Greenside Sand Shots, Penalties 0–≥4. | One hole per screen; not worth capturing. |
| Rounds Played list | Me → Rounds Played | Sortable by score, frequency or date; filterable. What each row shows is unconfirmed. | Many rounds per screen, useful for a total-scores-only history pass. |

Legend, from help article 551 (updated 2026-08-10): double circle = eagle or better, circle = birdie, plain = par, square = bogey, double square = double bogey or worse, red starburst = **Max**. Max probably marks the net-double-bogey cap that arrived in July 2024 (unconfirmed). A black dot means one stroke received and a red dot one stroke given. A red corner flag marks the starting hole. An orange `*` means another player changed the score.

Checked against the worked examples: the Redwood front nine 4+4+4+8+4+7+5+6+6 = 48 and back nine 45 give 93. Course par 71 means +22. GIR 1/18 = 5.6%. FH 4/13 = 30.8% (so 13 holes are par 4 or 5). Putts 29/18 = 1.6. **Every one of these redundancies is used in the checks in section 5.**

Past rounds can be entered as a **total score only**, so the schema must allow an empty holes list. Stats are optional per hole, so there are two "missing" states: *not recorded* (cell visible but empty) and *not visible* (not captured).

**Recommended capture (3–4 screenshots per round):** 1) the Round Summary top half; 2) Full Scorecard Scores, in landscape if one screen holds 9 holes, otherwise portrait swipes that overlap by at least one hole; 3) Full Scorecard Stats, same way; 4) Benchmarks. Leave the phone at native resolution: no zooming and no cropping.

## 2. Vision API limits and cost

- **Formats:** JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP only; **HEIC is not supported**. iOS screenshots are already PNG. HEIC photos from the camera or Photos export need converting: `sips -s format png in.heic --out out.png` (verified on this Mac: sips reads heic and writes png/jpeg) or `pillow_heif.register_heif_opener()` and then `Image.open(...).save(..., "PNG")`.
- **Limits:** 8000x8000 px per image; ≤10 MB base64 per image; ≤32 MB per request; ≤600 images per request on 1M-context models. Above 20 images in one request, every image must be ≤2000 px. Keep each round to 20 images or fewer and this never applies. Several multi-MB PNGs in base64 (which adds 33%) can get close to 32 MB. Re-encode to PNG/WebP, or JPEG at quality 90 or higher, or upload through the Files API and pass the `file_id`.
- **Resolution:** tokens = ceil(w/28)·ceil(h/28). Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 are in the high-res tier (2576 px long edge, 4784 tokens). iPhone 12–14 (1170x2532): 3,822 tokens, not resized. iPhone 15/16 (1179x2556): 3,956, not resized. 16 Pro/17/17 Pro (1206x2622) → 1185x2576: 3,956. Pro Max (1320x2868) → 1186x2576: 3,956. Landscape works the same way. Haiku 4.5 (standard tier) → about 723x1568, 1,456 tokens. **Don't** stitch swipes into one long image: 1206x6000 → 518x2576. Optionally pre-resize with Anthropic's `resized_size()` so the image sent is exactly the image Claude sees.
- **Per-round cost** (6 images ≈ 26.7K input tokens including about 3K of prompt; 3–8K output including thinking):

| Images | claude-opus-5 | Opus batch | claude-sonnet-5 | Sonnet batch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | $0.17–0.29 | $0.08–0.15 | $0.07–0.12 | $0.03–0.06 |
| 6 | $0.21–0.33 | $0.10–0.17 | $0.08–0.13 | $0.04–0.07 |
| 8 | $0.25–0.37 | $0.12–0.19 | $0.10–0.15 | $0.05–0.07 |

A 200-round backfill costs about $20–37 on Opus in batch, or $8–15 on Sonnet in batch. Prompt caching barely matters here, though the system prompt meets the cache minimum (512 tokens on Opus 5, 1024 on Sonnet 5).

## 3. Pipeline

```
screenshots (PNG) → sha256 / pHash dedupe → [optional] screen-type triage + round grouping
 → one Claude request per round (all images, 'Image N:' labels, images before the text)
 → ExtractedRound (Pydantic)  → raw JSON stored (re-validate without re-calling)
 → deterministic validators (+ optional ocrmac digit cross-check)
 → auto-accept | review queue (flagged cells) → corrections saved as patches (= eval ground truth)
 → derived stats (up&down, sand saves, SG-lite) → SQLite → static dashboard
```

Store the model, prompt_version, schema_version, `usage` and cost on every extraction run.

## 4. Wire schema, no nullables (Pydantic v2; `client.messages.parse(output_format=ExtractedRound)`)

Design rules come from the API limits: at most **16 union-typed** and **24 optional** parameters, and no min/max. So **every field is required**, integers use **-1 for unknown**, text uses **""**, and categorical fields carry explicit `not_visible` / `not_recorded` values. There are **no `Optional[...]`** fields (each would become an `anyOf`) and **no `Field(ge=...)`** constraints; those checks happen in the validator so a bad value can't fail the whole parse. Enum values are lowercase snake_case because enum capitalization isn't guaranteed.

```python
from typing import Literal
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

ScreenType = Literal["round_summary", "full_scorecard_scores", "full_scorecard_stats",
                     "benchmarks", "round_stats", "rounds_list", "gps_hole", "other"]
HoleField = Literal["par", "par_secondary", "yardage", "stroke_index", "stroke_index_secondary",
                    "strokes", "score_symbol", "net_strokes", "stroke_dots", "putts", "fairway",
                    "gir", "gir_miss", "chips", "sand_shots", "penalties"]
Conf = Literal["high", "medium", "low"]

class ImageInfo(BaseModel):
    image_index: int = Field(description="1-based index matching the 'Image N:' label")
    screen_type: ScreenType
    orientation: Literal["portrait", "landscape"]
    first_hole_visible: int = Field(description="Lowest hole number with a visible column; -1 if none")
    last_hole_visible: int = Field(description="Highest hole number with a visible column; -1 if none")
    problems: str = Field(description="Cut-off rows, glare, overlays, another player's card, etc. '' if none")

class HoleRow(BaseModel):
    hole_number: int
    par: int = Field(description="Printed par. For an 'x/y' men's/women's pair use x. -1 if not visible")
    par_secondary: int = Field(description="y of an 'x/y' par pair, else -1")
    yardage: int = Field(description="Yardage for the played tee, -1 if not visible")
    stroke_index: int = Field(description="18Birdies 'Handicap' row value (1-18); x of an 'x/y' pair; -1 if not visible")
    stroke_index_secondary: int = Field(description="y of an 'x/y' handicap pair, else -1")
    strokes: int = Field(description="Gross strokes for the requested player; -1 if blank/not played/not visible")
    score_symbol: Literal["none", "circle", "double_circle", "square", "double_square", "max_star", "not_visible"]
    net_strokes: int = Field(description="Net row value if shown, else -1")
    stroke_dots: int = Field(description="Count of black 'receive a stroke' dots on this hole; negative count for red 'give' dots; -1 if the area is not visible")
    putts: int = Field(description="-1 if not recorded or not visible (see uncertain/not_visible rules)")
    fairway: Literal["hit", "left", "right", "short", "long", "miss", "not_applicable", "not_recorded", "not_visible"]
    gir: Literal["hit", "miss", "not_recorded", "not_visible"]
    gir_miss: Literal["left", "right", "short", "long", "no_chance", "none", "not_visible"]
    chips: int
    sand_shots: int = Field(description="Greenside sand shots")
    penalties: int
    stats_visibility: Literal["visible", "not_captured"] = Field(description="Whether a Stats-view column for this hole was in any image; lets code tell -1=not recorded from -1=not captured")
    confidence: Conf
    uncertain_fields: list[HoleField]
    derived_fields: list[HoleField] = Field(description="Fields filled by inference, e.g. par from score symbol")
    source_images: list[int]

class DisplayedTotals(BaseModel):
    gross: int; net: int; front_nine: int; back_nine: int
    to_par_text: str = Field(description="Exactly as printed, e.g. '+22', 'E', '-1'; '' if not visible")
    par_front: int; par_back: int; yardage_front: int; yardage_back: int
    total_putts: int; fairways_hit: int; greens_in_regulation: int; penalties: int
    pars_or_better: int; holes_3plus_putts: int
    gir_pct_text: str; fh_pct_text: str; putts_per_hole_text: str
    up_down_text: str; sand_saves_text: str

class ExtractedRound(BaseModel):
    images: list[ImageInfo]
    player_name: str
    other_players_visible: list[str]
    course_name: str
    course_subname: str
    date_played_text: str = Field(description="Verbatim, e.g. '11/12/23'")
    date_played_iso: str = Field(description="YYYY-MM-DD (US month/day order) or ''")
    tee_name: str
    tee_total_yards: int
    course_par: int
    course_rating: float = Field(description="-1 if not shown")
    slope_rating: int
    duration_minutes: int
    holes_in_round: int = Field(description="9 or 18; -1 if unknown")
    starting_hole: int = Field(description="Hole with the red starting-hole flag, else 1; -1 if unknown")
    handicap_before_text: str
    handicap_after_text: str
    weather_text: str
    holes: list[HoleRow] = Field(description="One row per hole seen, ascending; empty if only a total is shown")
    displayed: DisplayedTotals
    overall_confidence: Conf
    issues: list[str] = Field(description="Conflicts between images, cut-offs, anything a reviewer should know")
```

After parsing, convert to a domain model: -1/""/not_visible → `None`, parse `to_par_text` ("E" means 0), keep the raw values, and compute derived fields in code.
- **GIR if it wasn't recorded:** strokes − putts ≤ par − 2.
- **Up-and-down:** a chance when gir == miss and chips + sand ≥ 1; made when chips + sand == 1 and putts ≤ 1. 18Birdies' own definition is unconfirmed, so compare against the Benchmarks value.
- **Sand save:** sand_shots ≥ 1 and the sand shot plus putts ≤ 2.
- **Scoring:** score to par, and net strokes as strokes − dots.

## 5. Prompt

**System prompt** (frozen, so it can be cached):

```
You transcribe golf round data from screenshots of the 18Birdies iPhone app into the given JSON schema. Accuracy beats completeness: never guess a value that is not legible — use the sentinel and flag it.

Screens you may see:
• Round Summary: date (M/D/YY), course name (+ subname in parentheses), "Course Par", "Tee: <name> <yards> yds", "Duration", "To Par", "Gross/Net". A condensed grid: row 1 = holes 1–9 with the front-nine total at the far right; row 2 = holes 10–18 with the back-nine total. Hole numbers are small, above each score. Par is NOT printed here.
• Full Scorecard – Scores view: columns = holes (+ Out/In/Tot); rows include Par and Handicap (= stroke index) and each player's Gross and Net. "4/5" means Men's/Women's values: first number → par / stroke_index, second → par_secondary / stroke_index_secondary. Small black dots on a hole = strokes received (count them); red dots = strokes given (record as a negative count).
• Full Scorecard – Stats view: per-hole Score, Fairway Hit, Green in Regulation, Putts, Chip Shots, Greenside Sand Shots, Penalties.
• Benchmarks: use ONLY the "THIS ROUND" column; ignore averages and percentiles.
• Screens may be portrait or landscape; scorecards are often split across horizontally swiped screenshots that overlap.

Score symbols (18Birdies legend): double circle = eagle or better; circle = birdie; no mark = par; square = bogey; double square = double bogey or worse; red starburst = Max. Record the symbol you SEE in score_symbol, independently of par.

Rules:
1. Transcribe, don't compute. Put printed totals in `displayed` exactly as shown; never fill a total by adding holes.
2. Sentinels: -1 for integers, "" for text. Use not_visible when the relevant part of the screen was not captured or is unreadable; use not_recorded when the cell is visible but empty or a dash. Set stats_visibility per hole.
3. Extract only the requested player's card; list other names in other_players_visible.
4. Merge overlapping screenshots: exactly one row per hole, ascending. If images disagree on a cell, use the clearer image, set that hole's confidence to low, add the field to uncertain_fields, and describe the conflict in issues.
5. If only a total score is shown (no hole grid), return an empty holes list.
6. Par from symbol: only when par is printed nowhere, you may infer par from strokes + symbol (plain → par = strokes; square → strokes−1; circle → strokes+1). List 'par' in derived_fields. Double symbols are ambiguous — leave -1.
7. uncertain_fields must list every field you are not sure of (blur, occlusion, 1/7, 3/8, 5/6, single vs double outline). confidence=high only if every field on that hole was read clearly.
8. Fairway on par 3s = not_applicable. ✓ → hit; left/right arrow or L/R → left/right; bare ✗ → miss.
9. After transcribing, compare your hole values with the printed totals (Out/In/Gross, Benchmarks). If they disagree, look again; if they still disagree, keep what you read and explain in issues. Never change a read value to make totals match.
```

**User turn:** for each image, send `{"type":"text","text":"Image N:"}` and then the image block. After all images: `"Extract the round for player: <name as shown in app>. Screens were captured in this order: <optional hints>."`

**Call:**
```python
resp = client.messages.parse(
    model="claude-opus-5",          # or "claude-sonnet-5" for about 40% of the cost
    max_tokens=16000,
    thinking={"type": "adaptive"},
    output_config={"effort": "high"},   # measure "medium" too
    system=SYSTEM_PROMPT,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": blocks}],
    output_format=ExtractedRound,
)
if resp.stop_reason in ("max_tokens", "refusal"):
    ...  # retry / flag
round_ = resp.parsed_output
```
Grammar constraints apply only to the final answer, so adaptive thinking can still check the sums first. The compiled grammar is cached for 24 hours after last use, so the first call is slower. For batches, pass `output_config={"format": {"type": "json_schema", "schema": transform_schema(TypeAdapter(ExtractedRound).json_schema())}, ...}` and validate with `ExtractedRound.model_validate_json`. Test the schema once to make sure it doesn't hit "Schema is too complex".

## 6. Deterministic checks

These run in plain code after extraction. **E** = error: send to review. **W** = warning: send to review if two or more fire, or with any low-confidence field. **I** = info.

| # | Rule | Sev |
|---|---|---|
| V1 | Hole numbers unique and consecutive; 9 or 18 rows (or 0 if total only); matches holes_in_round | E |
| V2 | Σ strokes holes 1–9 = displayed.front_nine; Σ 10–18 = back_nine; front + back = gross | E |
| V3 | gross − course_par = parsed to_par_text | E |
| V4 | Σ par = course_par; Σ par front/back = par_front/par_back (when every par is known) | E |
| V5 | par ∈ {3,4,5,6}; course_par within 27–37 for 9 holes or 54–76 for 18 | E |
| V6 | stroke_index values distinct and within 1..18 (a full 1..18 set on 18 holes; 9-hole cards often use only odd or only even values) | E |
| V7 | Symbol matches strokes − par: none → 0, circle → −1, double_circle → ≤ −2, square → +1, double_square → ≥ +2 (max_star: skip) | E (a mismatch means strokes or par was misread) |
| V8 | 1 ≤ strokes ≤ par + 10; 0 ≤ putts ≤ 6; chips, sand and penalties within 0–6 | E |
| V9 | putts ≤ strokes − 1 | E |
| V10 | strokes ≥ 1 + putts + chips + sand_shots + penalties (when all are known) | W |
| V11 | fairway = not_applicable exactly when par == 3; FH% denominator = number of par-4/5 holes | E / W |
| V12 | GIR agrees with scoring: gir == hit ⇒ strokes − putts ≤ par − 2; gir == miss ⇒ strokes − putts > par − 2 (putts from the fringe can break this) | W |
| V13 | Benchmarks totals: Σ putts = total_putts; count(fairway == hit) = fairways_hit; count(gir == hit) = greens_in_regulation; Σ penalties = penalties; count(strokes ≤ par) = pars_or_better; count(putts ≥ 3) = holes_3plus_putts; percentages within ±0.1 of the recomputed value | E |
| V14 | gross − net = Σ stroke_dots (Σ(strokes − net_strokes) per hole when the net row is known) | W |
| V15 | Σ yardage = tee_total_yards; yardage_front + yardage_back = tee_total_yards | W |
| V16 | Date parses, is not in the future, and is after Shane's first 18Birdies round; course name matches a known course (fuzzy) | W |
| V17 | Any uncertain_fields, confidence low, a non-empty `issues` list, or overall_confidence ≠ high | W |
| V18 | Optional OCR check: each 9-hole score row appears in order among the ocrmac tokens on that row; every printed total is found by OCR | W |

Auto-accept only when there are no E flags, at most one W flag, and no low-confidence holes.

## 7. Duplicate detection

1. **File level:** skip files whose sha256 is already stored. Treat images whose perceptual hash is within Hamming distance 6 as re-captures of the same screen and keep the higher-resolution copy.
2. **Round key:** `(date_iso, norm(course_name + subname), norm(tee_name))`, plus a fingerprint = sha1 of the tuple of 18 stroke values (total-only rounds use the gross score).
   - Same key and same fingerprint: a duplicate. **Merge field by field**: prefer read values over -1 and higher-confidence values, and keep who supplied each value, so a Summary captured today and Stats captured later end up as one round.
   - Same key, 16–17 holes equal: a likely re-capture after an edit, or a misread. Send to review with a diff and default to the newer capture.
   - Same key, stroke sequences differ in 3 or more holes: a legitimate second round that day. Keep both.
   - Same fingerprint and course, different date: probably a misread date. Send to review.
3. Record the screenshot capture time and use it only for grouping; it is not the date of play.

## 8. Human review and correction

- **v1:** write the flagged cells to a CSV/YAML (round, hole, field, value, reason, image#). Shane edits it and re-imports.
- **v2:** a local FastAPI (or Streamlit) page with the screenshots on the left and an editable 18-column grid on the right. Error cells are red and warning or uncertain cells amber; keyboard navigation; one "accept round" action.
- **Targeted re-read before a human looks:** for up to about 5 flagged cells, send only the relevant image with a narrow question ("Hole 7, Putts row: what digit?") and a tiny schema. That costs about 4K tokens, roughly $0.02 on Opus. Accept the answer if both reads agree; otherwise ask Shane.
- **Store every correction** as a patch: `{round_id, hole, field, model_value, corrected_value, reason, prompt_version, model}`. Corrected rounds become the **ground-truth set** used to compare models, prompts and effort levels by field-level accuracy, and to catch problems when 18Birdies changes its UI.
- **Status machine:** extracted → needs_review | auto_accepted → accepted (only accepted rounds reach the dashboard; others show as "pending").

## 9. Cross-check and fallback notes

- **ocrmac:** `ocrmac.OCR(path, recognition_level="accurate", language_preference=["en-US"]).recognize()` returns (text, conf, [x, y, w, h]) normalized, **origin at the lower left**. Flip y, bucket tokens into rows (tolerance about 0.6 of the median token height), sort by x, and use the hole-number header row to find columns. It checks digits only; it cannot see the symbols, the ✓/✗ icons or the dots.
- **macOS 26 RecognizeDocumentsRequest** (Swift): returns table cells with row and column indices. It would be a stronger grid check than row bucketing, but needs our own small Swift command-line tool.
- **Refusal fallback:** for interactive Opus 5 calls, the server-side `fallbacks` beta can be added. It isn't needed for scorecards and can't be used in batches.
