Visual tokens = ceil(w/28)*ceil(h/28). 'Claude 4.7 and later' models, including Opus 5 and Sonnet 5, use the high-res tier (2576 px long edge, 4784 tokens), so an iPhone portrait screenshot costs about 3,956 tokens with almost no downscaling. Haiku 4.5 is standard tier (1568/1568; about 1,456 tokens).
Per round (4–8 screenshots): about $0.17–0.37 on claude-opus-5 and $0.07–0.15 on claude-sonnet-5; the Batch API halves both.

Structured outputs support images and batches. They don't support minimum/maximum/maxItems. Limits: 24 optional parameters and 16 union-typed (anyOf/nullable) parameters per request. The Python SDK strips unsupported constraints and checks them on the client. Enum capitalization is not guaranteed. The grammar applies only to the final output, not to thinking.
The proposed all-required, sentinel-based ExtractedRound schema compiles without a 'Schema is too complex' error (not tested).

18Birdies scorecard legend: double circle eagle, circle birdie, plain par, square bogey, double square double bogey, red starburst Max, black/red dots = strokes received/given, '4/5' = men's/women's par or hole handicap.

The 18Birdies Round Summary shows date, course, course par, tee + yards, duration, To Par, Gross/Net and all 18 hole scores with symbols plus front/back totals on one screen, but not per-hole par or putts.
The Full Scorecard has a Scores/Stats toggle. Portrait needs horizontal swipes; landscape (since July 2024) gives a wider view, but how many holes it shows is unconfirmed.

Classic Score Entry records score, putts, fairway, GIR, penalties, chips and greenside sand shots per hole. Fairway misses record Left/Short/Right; GIR misses record Left/Long/Right/Short/No chance. Up & down and sand saves are computed stats.

The Benchmarks screen shows This Round totals (gross, net, front/back, par or better, FH, GIR, putts per hole, total putts, 3+ putt holes, up & down, sand saves, penalties). They can be used as checksums.
18Birdies can't export rounds to CSV, but its 'Download Your Account Data' page offers an archive (login required) said to include rounds. The archive's format is unknown.

verdicts.claim: Structured outputs: work with images and batches; no minimum/maximum/maxItems; limits of 24 optional and 16 union-typed parameters; the Python SDK strips unsupported constraints and validates them on the client; enum capitalization is not guaranteed; the grammar applies only to the final output, not thinking
verdicts.evidence: All of this is in the raw doc (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs.md): an 'Explicit limits' table (20 strict tools, 24 optional params, 16 union-typed params); 'Not supported' (numerical constraints like minimum/maximum/multipleOf, minLength/maxLength, array constraints beyond minItems 0/1); SDK-validated constraints 'stripped from the wire schema... validated against the response'; an 'Invalid outputs' capitalization caveat ('Compare enum values case-insensitively'); 'Grammars apply only to Claude's direct output, not... thinking'. It lists 'Works with: Batch processing... 50% discount' and 'Extract data from images or text' as a use case. supportedModels includes claude-opus-5-5, claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5 and claude-haiku-4-5. Grammar cache is 24 h from last use. The only incompatibilities are Citations and prefill.
verdicts.correction: One real gap in the design: client.messages.parse() calls TypeAdapter.validate_json() without catching errors (anthropic-sdk-python src/anthropic/lib/_parse/_response.py). If the model returns 'Hit' for an enum declared as 'hit', the whole call raises instead of returning raw JSON. Lowercase snake_case lowers the risk (the doc says drift usually hits a word after a space) but does not remove it. Use messages.create with output_config.format=transform_schema(...), plus a case-insensitive BeforeValidator. That also gives interactive and batch calls the same code path and keeps the raw text. Separately, I confirmed that parse() merges output_config={'effort':...} with output_format (messages.py lines ~1215–1223), so the snippet as written is valid.

verification.missed_options:
1) The 18Birdies account-data archive is a machine-readable JSON (18Birdies_archive.json), not an unknown blob. Its rounds[] hold holeStrokes (per-hole gross), strokes, score (to-par), timestamp, clubId and aggregate FH/GIR/putts with miss-direction counts; clubData maps clubId to course name. Sources: https://github.com/chrisdecali/golf-reports/blob/main/ingest/pull_18birdies.py (Jun 2026), which says '18Birdies has no usable API; this is the supported way to get your data', and a sample committed Dec 2025 in github.com/ericlu28/18birdies-wrapped. I read only its key names; it holds a third party's personal data and should not be reused. A hybrid design follows: the archive covers scores for all history, and Claude vision is only needed for per-hole par/stroke index (one Full Scorecard capture per course/tee) and per-hole putts/FH/GIR.

2) The model lineup changed on Sep 22, 2026. claude-opus-5-5 is current at $4/$20, with adaptive thinking always on, default effort medium, and forced tool use not supported. claude-opus-5 is now legacy (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/opus-5-5/overview, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/opus-5/overview). This contradicts the orchestrator's shared context.

3) Per-image `transformations: {"oversized_image": "error"}` guarantees Claude never silently downscales a screenshot (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/vision-coordinates).

4) messages.parse() raises on any Pydantic validation failure, including enum case drift. Prefer messages.create + output_config.format (transform_schema) + manual, case-insensitive validation, which also matches the batch path (anthropic-sdk-python src/anthropic/lib/_parse/_response.py; capitalization caveat in https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs).

5) Ingestion automation: osxphotos (MIT, v0.77.1 on 2026-09-23, supports macOS 26 with 'limited testing') can pull new screenshots from the Mac Photos library (its templates include a 'screenshot' media type; I did not verify the exact filter flag), with --update/--only-new for incremental runs. Caveat: Photos may not download original screenshots when iCloud 'Optimize Storage' is on (https://github.com/RhetTbull/osxphotos).

6) iOS 26 HDR screen-capture format saves screenshots as HEIC (https://www.idownloadblog.com/2025/09/20/take-hdr-screen-capture-ios/), so the ingest step must handle HEIC.

7) 18Birdies' 'Share Scorecard' produces one image with all 18 scores and symbols, course, tee yardage, rating/slope (e.g., '130.0/73.8') and starting hole. It can go to any app through the share sheet (https://help.18birdies.com/article/249-can-i-email-a-scorecard-to-myself; 2020 image file-BHiAT9p9CQ.png). It is an alternative capture that adds rating/slope, but still has no per-hole par.

8) 18Birdies has a per-hole Notes feature: notes persist on a hole across rounds, are shown on the full Scorecard/Stats card, and are hidden in Feed views (https://help.18birdies.com/article/543-using-notes; https://help.18birdies.com/article/657-data-missing-from-the-scorecard-or-round-summary). That matters for the notes/timeline part of the app.

9) 18Birdies settings affect data meaning: 'Automatic Stats Calculation' (stats computed from score and putts) and optional 'Missed GIR & Fairway Details' (https://help.18birdies.com/article/728-tracking-and-understanding-golf-statistics). The published Up & Down / Sand Save definitions are in https://help.18birdies.com/article/788-understanding-course-round-stats.

10) Strava's official MCP connector (https://mcp.strava.com/mcp; launched Jun 1, 2026; read-only; Strava subscribers; Claude-only; tools include list_activities, get_activity_performance, get_activity_streams) is the only policy-compliant way to get Strava data into Claude (https://support.strava.com/en-us/articles/15401531-strava-mcp-connector; https://www.strava.com/legal/api_policy §3.5). It lists no photo tool, so it cannot deliver the 18Birdies graphic.

11) The MCP registry has no 18Birdies connector (searched 'strava', 'golf', '18birdies').
verification.corrected_bottom_line:
Claude vision plus structured outputs is a sound, cheap way to read 18Birdies screenshots, and most of the researcher's API facts check out: formats, limits, token math, structured-output limits, Batch and cache figures. Four corrections:

(1) Shane should request the official 'Download Your Account Data' archive first. It is a JSON file with per-hole gross strokes for every round, plus per-round FH/GIR/putts aggregates and course names. That makes a screenshot backfill of scores unnecessary. Vision is then needed only for per-hole par/stroke index (once per course/tee) and optional per-hole putts/FH/GIR, and possibly for rounds played after the archive.

(2) Use claude-opus-5-5 ($4/$20, current since Sep 22, 2026; Opus 5 is legacy), or claude-sonnet-5 ($2/$10) with Opus as the fallback. That works out to about $0.14–0.30 per round on Opus 5.5 and roughly half in batch. Call messages.create with output_config.format and validate the enums case-insensitively yourself, because parse() raises on any mismatch.

(3) The 18Birdies screens have changed again. The April 2025 Round Summary uses a 'Basic Stats' layout, the help article describing the Scores/Stats scorecard toggle is gone, and the legend art is from 2019. The prompt and checks have to be built from Shane's own current screenshots, including landscape. Also handle HEIC, because iOS 26 HDR screenshots are saved that way.

research.summary:
Use a small JavaScript for Automation (JXA) script of your own, run with osascript. It reads one dedicated "Golf" folder in Apple Notes and returns each note's id, title, plaintext, creation date, modification date and a password-protected flag. It needs only the one-time macOS Automation prompt ("Terminal wants to control Notes"). It does not need Full Disk Access, an MCP server, or a third-party dependency, and it never has to decode the NoteStore.sqlite protobuf format. I checked this Mac's own Notes scripting dictionary (macOS 26.5.1): it exposes plaintext, creation date, modification date and password protected, but no tags. Locked notes cannot be read by any method short of the password, so the pipeline records their metadata and skips the body.

The ready-made options are weaker. simonw's apple-notes-to-sqlite (now dogsheep/) has had one release, v0.1 in March 2023. It has an open bug where it decodes text as mac_roman and corrupts non-ASCII characters, it cannot sync incrementally, and it stores the HTML body, which carries inline base64 images. Reading NoteStore.sqlite directly needs Full Disk Access and breaks when Apple changes the schema. Apple Notes MCP servers are good for exploring notes interactively in Claude; the most active is sweetrb/apple-notes-mcp (133 stars, v2.9.30 released today). They are the wrong basis for a batch pipeline.

Apple Notes has no per-paragraph timestamps, so a running log is only as datable as the dates Shane types into it. The extraction design therefore has the LLM copy the date words and describe them in structured fields ("last Tuesday" becomes weekday=tue, rel=last, anchored to the note's creation date or to its entry header). Python then does all the date arithmetic, because LLMs make off-by-one-day errors on date math. Each event is identified by a hash of (note, type, verbatim excerpt), with an extraction cache and a separate review layer, so re-syncing is idempotent and never overwrites Shane's edits. Two quick-add paths keep future dates clean: a CLI command, and an iPhone Shortcut that appends ISO-dated lines to a "Golf Log" note.

Other sources all work if his notes live elsewhere. Google Docs: Drive files.export, which supports text/markdown. Notion: the API, including a page-as-markdown endpoint and a per-block created_time. Markdown files work directly. Google Keep can only be read from a Takeout export, because its API is Workspace-only. Because Apple Notes can only be read on the Mac, notes ingestion has to run locally, not in GitHub Actions. Also, GitHub Pages sites are public even from private repos, which matters for injury notes.

options.name: A. Own JXA script via osascript (RECOMMENDED for Apple Notes)
options.how_it_works: A script of about 40 lines, notes_dump.js, run as `osascript -l JavaScript notes_dump.js meta Golf`. It fetches metadata for every note in the Golf folder in bulk: `f.notes.id()`, `.name()`, `.creationDate()`, `.modificationDate()`, `.passwordProtected()` each come back as a JS array in one Apple Event. It returns JSON on stdout. Plaintext is then fetched with `Notes.notes.byId(id).plaintext()`, only for unlocked notes whose modification date changed since the last sync. Python calls it with subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, encoding='utf-8'), then normalizes the text, hashes it and upserts it into SQLite. research.design_notes:
# Golf notes → timeline: design

## 0. Recommendation summary
1. Move golf notes into one **iCloud** Apple Notes folder named `Golf`. Notes kept "On My iPhone" never reach the Mac.
2. Ingest the folder with a JXA script of our own, called through `osascript` from Python. The only permission needed is Automation (Terminal → Notes). No Full Disk Access, no MCP, no third-party package.
3. Store everything in local SQLite: `source_docs`, `extraction_runs`, `events`, `event_reviews`.
4. Extract with `claude-sonnet-5` through structured outputs (the Pydantic model in §4). The LLM **describes** each date; Python **resolves** it (§6).
5. Make the pipeline idempotent with a content hash per note, an extraction cache keyed on (hash, prompt_version, schema_version, model), and stable event ids built from the verbatim excerpt. Keep human review as a separate overlay table.
6. Review with a local CLI (or a YAML file). Only accepted or auto-accepted events go to the dashboard export.
7. Add quick-add paths going forward: `golf add ...` and an iPhone Shortcut that writes `YYYY-MM-DD | text` lines into a "Golf Log" note.
8. Notes ingestion runs **on the Mac** (a manual `make sync` or a wrapped launchd job). GitHub Actions cannot read Apple Notes. Commit only the exported `timeline_events.json`, and consider privacy (§14).

## 1. Apple Notes adapter

### notes_dump.js
```js
// usage: osascript -l JavaScript notes_dump.js meta "Golf"
//        osascript -l JavaScript notes_dump.js body "<note id>"
function run(argv) {
  const Notes = Application("Notes");
  const mode = argv[0], arg = argv[1];
  if (mode === "meta") {
    const out = [];
    // app-level folders; verify on first run whether nested sub-folders are included (unconfirmed)
    const folders = Notes.folders.whose({ name: arg })();
    for (const f of folders) {
      const ns = f.notes;                       // bulk property reads = 1 Apple Event each
      const ids = ns.id(), names = ns.name(), cr = ns.creationDate(),
            mo = ns.modificationDate(), locked = ns.passwordProtected();
      for (let i = 0; i < ids.length; i++) out.push({
        id: ids[i], title: names[i], folder: f.name(),
        created: cr[i].toISOString(), modified: mo[i].toISOString(), locked: locked[i] });
    }
    return JSON.stringify(out);
  }
  if (mode === "body") {
    const n = Notes.notes.byId(arg);
    return JSON.stringify({ id: arg, plaintext: n.plaintext() });   // plaintext, NOT body (HTML inlines base64 images)
  }
}
```
Python wrapper: `subprocess.run(["osascript","-l","JavaScript",JS,mode,arg], capture_output=True, encoding="utf-8", timeout=120, check=True)`, then `json.loads(stdout)`. Always decode as UTF-8; apple-notes-to-sqlite's mac_roman bug corrupted 31% of notes.

### Normalization and hash
```python
def normalize(t):
    t = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", t).replace("\r\n","\n").replace(" ","\n")
    t = t.replace("￼", "")  # attachment placeholder char, if present (defensive; unconfirmed)
    t = "\n".join(l.rstrip() for l in t.split("\n"))
    return re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", t).strip()
content_hash = sha256(normalize(text).encode()).hexdigest()
```
Convert timestamps from UTC to the configured local zone (e.g. America/New_York) **before** taking `.date()`. A note written at 11:30 pm is the local day, not the UTC day.

### Gotchas
- Locked notes: store the metadata row with `status='locked'` and skip the body. Their bodies are end-to-end encrypted and cannot be read without the password.
- Id stability: if an id disappears and a new id appears with the same `created_at` and `content_hash`, re-key it instead of treating it as delete plus add.
- Deleted notes: an id missing from `meta` gets `deleted_at` set. Keep its events but hide them. Don't cascade-delete reviewed events.
- Bulk-import detection: if many notes share the same `created_at` to the second (e.g. imported from Evernote), creation dates are unreliable. Flag `created_unreliable` so relative dates resolve with precision=`inferred`.
- Scheduling: the first run must be interactive to accept the Automation prompt. For launchd, wrap the job in an `osacompile` app so the TCC grant sticks to a stable identity.
- Tags such as #golf are not in the scripting dictionary. Use the folder, not tags.

## 2. Other adapters (all emit the same SourceDoc)
| source | list/changed | text | per-entry date help |
|---|---|---|---|
| Google Docs | Drive files.list (folder, modifiedTime) | files.export text/markdown (≤10 MB) | revisions (unconfirmed) |
| Notion | search / database query, last_edited_time | GET /v1/pages/{id}/markdown or recursive block walk | **block.created_time** → date_source `block_created` |
| Markdown / txt | glob + mtime | file | front-matter / filename date; `git blame` per line |
| Keep | Takeout JSON | textContent | createdTimestampUsec / userEditedTimestampUsec |
| Manual | CLI / YAML | text | explicit date |

## 3. Storage (SQLite)
```sql
CREATE TABLE source_docs(
  doc_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,          -- 'applenotes:<x-coredata id>' | 'gdoc:<id>' | 'notion:<id>' | 'md:<relpath>' | 'manual:<uuid>'
  source TEXT, title TEXT, folder TEXT,
  created_at TEXT, modified_at TEXT,  -- ISO-8601 with offset, local tz
  text TEXT, content_hash TEXT,
  status TEXT CHECK(status IN ('active','locked','deleted')),
  flags TEXT,                         -- JSON: ["created_unreliable", ...]
  first_seen_at TEXT, last_synced_at TEXT, deleted_at TEXT);

CREATE TABLE extraction_runs(
  run_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, doc_id TEXT, content_hash TEXT,
  model TEXT, prompt_version TEXT, schema_version TEXT,
  cache_key TEXT UNIQUE,             -- sha256(content_hash|prompt_version|schema_version|model|known_entities_hash)
  response_json TEXT, input_tokens INT, output_tokens INT, created_at TEXT);

CREATE TABLE events(
  event_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,         -- see §8
  doc_id TEXT, run_id TEXT,
  status TEXT CHECK(status IN ('pending','auto_accepted','accepted','rejected','superseded','orphaned')),
  event_type TEXT, is_planned INT,
  date TEXT, date_start TEXT, date_end TEXT,
  date_precision TEXT CHECK(date_precision IN ('exact','day','week','month','inferred')),
  date_source TEXT CHECK(date_source IN ('explicit_text','note_created','note_modified','relative_reference','log_position','block_created','manual')),
  date_expression TEXT,
  coach TEXT, location TEXT, location_kind TEXT, lesson_format TEXT, duration_minutes INT,
  focus_areas TEXT, drills TEXT, swing_thoughts TEXT, equipment TEXT, measurements TEXT, injury TEXT, goal_text TEXT,  -- JSON
  game_areas TEXT,                   -- denormalized distinct game_area list, for joining to stats
  summary TEXT, source_note_id TEXT, source_excerpt TEXT, line_start INT, line_end INT,
  excerpt_verified INT, confidence TEXT, review_reasons TEXT, flags TEXT,
  linked_round_id TEXT,              -- set when an on_course event matches an 18Birdies round date
  first_seen_run TEXT, last_seen_run TEXT, created_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT);

CREATE TABLE event_reviews(          -- human overlay; never written by the extractor
  event_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, decision TEXT CHECK(decision IN ('accept','reject','merge')),
  merged_into TEXT, edits_json TEXT,  -- RFC-7386 merge patch applied on read
  comment TEXT, reviewed_at TEXT);

CREATE VIEW timeline AS  -- events with review edits applied; export this
  SELECT ... FROM events e LEFT JOIN event_reviews r USING(event_id)
  WHERE (r.decision='accept') OR (e.status='auto_accepted' AND COALESCE(r.decision,'')<>'reject');
```

## 4. LLM-facing schema (Pydantic, used with `client.messages.parse`)
All fields are required but nullable, with no defaults. That keeps the grammar strict. Constraints such as length limits are stated in descriptions and enforced in post-validation.
```python
from enum import Enum
from typing import Literal, Optional
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
SCHEMA_VERSION = "timeline-v1"

class EventType(str, Enum):
    lesson="lesson"; practice="practice"; on_course="on_course"
    equipment_change="equipment_change"; fitting="fitting"; injury="injury"
    fitness="fitness"; goal="goal"; swing_thought="swing_thought"
    milestone="milestone"; other="other"

class GameArea(str, Enum):   # maps onto 18Birdies stats, see §13
    full_swing="full_swing"; driving="driving"; approach="approach"
    short_game="short_game"; bunker="bunker"; putting="putting"
    course_management="course_management"; mental="mental"
    physical="physical"; equipment="equipment"

Weekday = Literal["mon","tue","wed","thu","fri","sat","sun"]

class DateRef(BaseModel):
    expression: Optional[str] = Field(description="Date words copied verbatim from the note, e.g. '3/14', 'last Tuesday'. null if none.")
    kind: Literal["absolute","relative","header","none"]
    year: Optional[int]; month: Optional[int]; day: Optional[int]
    time_of_day: Optional[str] = Field(description="24h HH:MM if a time is written, else null")
    relative_anchor: Optional[Literal["note_created","entry_header"]]
    header_line: Optional[int] = Field(description="Line number of the entry header this date comes from / is relative to")
    offset_days: Optional[int] = Field(description="yesterday=-1, today=0, tomorrow=1, '3 days ago'=-3")
    weekday: Optional[Weekday]
    weekday_rel: Optional[Literal["last","this","next","unspecified"]]
    period: Optional[Literal["week","weekend","month","year"]]
    period_offset: Optional[int] = Field(description="'last week'=-1, 'two weeks ago'=-2, 'this month'=0")
    approximate: bool = Field(description="true for 'around', 'early May', 'a couple weeks ago'")
```

## 6. Deterministic date resolution (Python)
```python
def resolve_doc(extr, doc):
    created, modified = doc.created_local.date(), doc.modified_local.date()
    headers = resolve_headers(extr, created, modified)      # {line: Resolved}
    for ev in extr.events:
        r = resolve(ev.date, ev.is_planned, doc, headers, extr.note_kind)
        ...

def resolve(ref, planned, doc, headers, note_kind):
    if ref.kind == "header":
        h = headers.get(ref.header_line) or fail("bad_header_line")
        return h.with_source("explicit_text" if h.source=="explicit_text" else h.source)
    if ref.kind == "absolute":
        lo, hi = doc.created - 180d, doc.modified + (180d if planned else 7d)
        if ref.month and ref.day:
            d = pick_year(ref.month, ref.day, ref.year, lo, hi, prefer=doc.created)  # flag year_inferred if year None
            prec = "exact" if ref.time_of_day else "day"
            return widen(Resolved(d, d, d, prec, "explicit_text"), ref.approximate)
        if ref.month:
            s, e = month_bounds(pick_year(ref.month, 1, ref.year, lo, hi, doc.created), ref.month)
            return Resolved(mid(s, e), s, e, "month", "explicit_text")
    if ref.kind == "relative":
        anchor = headers[ref.header_line].date if ref.relative_anchor == "entry_header" else doc.created
        if ref.offset_days is not None: d = anchor + timedelta(ref.offset_days); out = day(d)
        elif ref.weekday:            out = day(weekday_resolve(anchor, ref.weekday, ref.weekday_rel, planned))
        elif ref.period == "week":   mon = anchor - timedelta(anchor.weekday()) + timedelta(weeks=ref.period_offset or 0); out = Resolved(mon+3d, mon, mon+6d, "week")
        elif ref.period == "weekend":sat = last_weekday(anchor, "sat", strict=True); out = Resolved(sat, sat, sat+1d, "week")
        elif ref.period == "month":  s, e = month_bounds(shift_month(anchor, ref.period_offset or 0)); out = Resolved(mid(s,e), s, e, "month")
        out.source = "relative_reference"
        if doc.flags has "created_unreliable" and ref.relative_anchor == "note_created": out.precision = "inferred"
        return widen(out, ref.approximate)       # day->week, week->month when approximate
    # kind == none
    if note_kind in ("single_entry", "mixed") : return Resolved(created, created, created, "day", "note_created")
    return log_position(ev, headers, doc)          # between neighbouring dated headers -> precision "inferred", source "log_position"
                                                   # if after the last dated entry: bounds [last_header, modified], source "note_modified"

def weekday_resolve(anchor, wd, rel, planned):
    t = WEEKDAYS.index(wd)
    if rel == "next" or (rel in ("unspecified", "this") and planned):
        return anchor + timedelta(days=((t - anchor.weekday() - 1) % 7) + 1)          # strictly after
    if rel == "this": return anchor - timedelta(anchor.weekday()) + timedelta(t)    # same Mon-Sun week
    back = ((anchor.weekday() - t - 1) % 7) + 1                                       # strictly before (1..7)
    d = anchor - timedelta(back)
    if rel == "last" and back < anchor.weekday() + 1: flag("ambiguous_last_weekday")  # 'last Tue' said on Thu: this week or prior?
    return d
```
**Header year inference for running logs:** allow a window lo=created-14d, hi=modified+1d. Walk the headers in log order (reversed if `reverse_chronological`). For each header, candidates = {date(y,m,d) for y in lo.year..hi.year within the window}. Keep candidates ≥ the previous header minus 3 days, pick the earliest, and flag `non_monotonic` or `out_of_window` when nothing fits. This handles Dec→Jan rollovers and logs that span several years.

**Cross-check:** `dateparser.parse(expression, settings={"RELATIVE_BASE": anchor_dt, "PREFER_DATES_FROM": "past"})`. If it disagrees with our resolution by more than the precision width, flag `date_disagreement`.

**Sanity flags:** resolved date > modified+1d and not planned → `future_date`. Resolved date < created-365d → `far_past`. Any flag forces `pending` review.

Precision definitions: **exact** = day and time known. **day** = calendar day. **week** = within a Mon–Sun week. **month** = within a month. **inferred** = no usable date text; estimated from metadata or position, with `date_start`/`date_end` as bounds. `date` is the point estimate (the midpoint for ranges).

## 7. Running logs
- Send the whole note, so the header context and coach carry across entries. Split only if the note exceeds about 15k tokens. Split at header lines detected by the regex `^\s*(\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}(/\d{2,4})?|\w{3,9}\.? \d{1,2}|\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\b` plus dateparser, and pass the previous segment's last header as context.
- Apple Notes stores no per-paragraph timestamps. An undated entry appended to a log is inherently imprecise (`log_position`/`note_modified`, precision `inferred`), which is why the quick-add Shortcut writes an ISO date on every line.

## 8. Idempotent incremental re-sync
```
sync():
  meta = jxa_meta("Golf")
  for m in meta:
    prev = docs.get(m.id)
    if m.locked: upsert(m, status='locked'); continue
    if prev and prev.modified_at == m.modified: continue            # cheap pre-filter
    text = normalize(jxa_body(m.id)); h = sha256(text)
    if prev and prev.content_hash == h: touch(prev); continue        # moved/pinned, same text
    upsert_doc(m, text, h); queue.add(m.id)
  mark_deleted(set(docs) - {m.id for m in meta})
  for doc in queue:
    key = sha256(h|PROMPT_VERSION|SCHEMA_VERSION|MODEL|entities_hash)
    extr = cache.get(key) or call_claude_and_store(doc, key)         # re-running never re-bills
    reconcile(doc, resolve_doc(validate(extr, doc), doc))
```
**Validation:** each excerpt must be a substring of the note after whitespace collapse; otherwise try a `difflib` best-window match at ratio ≥ 0.9, else set `excerpt_verified=0` and flag. Line ranges must be within bounds. Any header_line referenced must exist in entry_headers.

**Event id:** `sha256(doc_id | event_type | norm(excerpt) | ordinal)[:16]`, where `norm` = lowercase with collapsed whitespace, and `ordinal` distinguishes two events of the same type that share an excerpt. If an entry's text is unchanged, its id survives edits elsewhere in the note.

**Reconcile(doc, new_events):**
- Same id already present → update the machine fields and `last_seen_run`, and keep the status.
- New id → `pending`, or `auto_accepted` if it passes the policy in §9.
- Old id missing → if it was reviewed (accept or edits) it becomes `orphaned`, otherwise `superseded`. For each orphan, look for a new event of the same type in the same doc with excerpt similarity ≥ 0.8. If found, propose carrying the review over (shown in review, one keystroke to confirm).
- `event_reviews` is never touched by the extractor. Human edits are applied as a merge-patch overlay at read time.
- Bumping `PROMPT_VERSION` re-extracts everything through the same reconcile path, so reviews carry over wherever the excerpts are stable.

**Cross-note duplicates:** same event_type, dates overlapping within precision, and the same coach or equipment model → flag `possible_duplicate` with a pointer to the other event. Review can resolve it with `merge`.

## 9. Review step
- `golf sync` prints a summary such as "14 new events: 10 auto-accepted, 4 need review".
- `golf review` is a rich/questionary TUI. For each pending, orphaned or flagged event it shows: excerpt with note title, resolved date `2026-03-21 (day, relative_reference: 'last sat' ← header L004)`, the fields, and the flags. Keys: [a]ccept, [r]eject, [e]dit (opens $EDITOR on the event as YAML; the diff is saved as edits_json), [m]erge, [s]kip, [o]pen the note in Notes (`Notes.show`).
- The alternative with no TUI: `review/pending.yaml` is written, Shane edits it in VS Code, and `golf apply-review` merges it.
- Auto-accept policy (configurable): confidence=high AND excerpt_verified AND no flags AND date_source in {explicit_text, relative_reference} AND NOT approximate. On the **first backfill, review everything** to calibrate; later, audit a sample of 10% of auto-accepts.
- The dashboard exports only the `timeline` view. Pending events can appear in a "needs review" count.

## 10. Manual quick-add
1. `golf add "<free text>" [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--type lesson --coach "Mike Rossi" --focus putting]`. With only text, it creates a `manual:` SourceDoc (created = --date or now), runs the extractor, and sets status `accepted` (user-authored). With structured flags, it skips the LLM.
2. iPhone Shortcut "Golf log": Ask for Input (text) → Ask for Input (date, default Current Date) → Format Date `yyyy-MM-dd` → Text `"{date} | {text}"` → Find Notes (Name is "Golf Log", Limit 1) → Append to Note. Every line then carries an explicit ISO date.
3. `manual_events.yaml` for historical memories, e.g. `{type: fitting, date: 2024-05, precision: month, summary: "iron fitting", equipment: [...]}`.

## 11. Evaluation (small gold set)
Hand-label 15–20 notes, including 3 or more running logs. Match predicted events to gold events on (type, overlapping line range) using Hungarian matching. Report:
- event precision, recall and F1
- type accuracy
- date accuracy: the resolved date falls in the gold [start, end]; exact-day match rate
- coach, location and equipment exact match
- excerpt_verified rate

Run as a pytest regression on every PROMPT_VERSION or MODEL change. Target F1 ≥ 0.9 and date-in-range ≥ 0.95 before turning on auto-accept.

## 12. Cost (Sonnet 5, $2/$10 per MTok)
Estimated per note: about 3.5k input tokens (system prompt with example ≈2.5k, plus note and entities) and about 1–1.5k output tokens, so roughly $0.02. A 150-note backfill comes to about $3 (about $1.5 with the Batch API). Incremental syncs cost cents. Opus 5 is about 2.5 times that.

## 13. Joining the timeline to score analytics
GameArea → 18Birdies metric:
- driving → FIR%, penalties
- approach / full_swing → GIR%
- short_game / bunker → scrambling, up-and-down %
- putting → putts per round, 3-putts
- course_management → doubles-or-worse, penalties
- equipment (driver) → FIR% and driving distance

Overlay events as vertical rules on rolling-differential charts, colored by type. For each lesson or equipment change, compare the N rounds before and after on the matched metric. Use a Bayesian or bootstrap interval, because n is small, and call it descriptive, not causal. `on_course` events whose date matches a round get `linked_round_id`.

## 14. Privacy
- Note text (including injuries) goes to the Anthropic API at extraction time.
- GitHub Pages sites are public even from private repos, unless the owner is on Enterprise Cloud with private Pages. Either export only type, date, coach, focus areas and a short summary (drop excerpts and injury details), or keep the timeline page local.
- Store no tokens in the repo. Google and Notion tokens go in the macOS Keychain via `keyring`.

verdicts.claim: Claude structured outputs do not support minimum/maximum/minLength/maxLength/pattern or recursive schemas (minItems only 0 or 1). The Python SDK strips these, notes them in descriptions and validates client-side.

A separate 'Pattern support (regex)' accordion says simple regex IS supported (anchors, *, +, ?, simple {n,m}, classes, groups), but not backreferences, lookaround or \b. SDK source anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python src/anthropic/lib/_parse/_transform.py keeps only 'format' for strings and appends every other leftover key, including pattern, to the description.
verdicts.correction: The API does support simple `pattern`; the Python SDK's transform is what drops it into the description. More importantly, the researcher missed the documented 'Schema complexity limits'. They allow at most 24 optional parameters and at most 16 'parameters with union types' ('anyOf or type arrays (for example, "type": ["string","null"])') per request, and exceeding them returns 400 'Schema is too complex for compilation'. The SDK transform preserves anyOf, so each Optional[...] Pydantic field counts as a union parameter. The proposed NoteExtraction schema has about 30 nullable fields: 12 in DateRef, 7 in TimelineEvent, 4 in Equipment, 2 each in Drill, Measurement and Injury, and 1 in NoteExtraction. That is roughly twice the limit, so as written it will very likely be rejected.

3) Better date sources for lessons and gear: calendar events and email receipts. Lesson bookings and club or fitting orders usually leave exact-dated records: Google Calendar or Apple Calendar events, and booking or order-confirmation emails in Gmail. Joining those is more reliable than resolving 'last Tuesday'. Verify on the first run whether app-level `Notes.folders.whose({name:'Golf'})` includes nested folders, and handle duplicate 'Golf' folders across accounts.

7) Apple Journal is now on Mac in macOS 26, but Apple documents only PDF export (https://support.apple.com/guide/journal/print-and-export-entries-dev883fc2329/mac). It is a poor machine-readable source if Shane journals golf there.

verification.corrected_bottom_line:
The core recommendation holds: have Shane move his golf notes into one iCloud 'Golf' folder and read it with a small JXA script run through osascript, using only the Automation permission. The local Notes.sdef on macOS 26.5.1 confirms every field the design relies on: plaintext, creation and modification dates, password protected, and no tags. The Automation-only permission model, locked-note limits, launchd/TCC caveats, the Notion, Google Docs and Keep facts, the Citations incompatibility, and the privacy warning about GitHub Pages are all confirmed.

Two corrections matter:

1. The LLM extraction step (option M) will likely fail as written. Claude structured outputs allow at most 16 union-typed (nullable) parameters and 24 optional ones per request, and the proposed NoteExtraction Pydantic model has about 30 Optional fields. The schema needs redesigning, with required fields plus sentinel values, a flatter DateRef, or two passes, and a real test call, before 'works-today' is accurate. Also, `pattern` is supported by the API; only the Python SDK strips it.

2. sweetrb/apple-notes-mcp's incremental cursor (`list-recent-notes`) and its Markdown/HTML export both need Full Disk Access; they are not part of its AppleScript-only surface.

Also, the '31% of notes corrupted' figure for apple-notes-to-sqlite comes from an AI-written issue comment. The mac_roman decode in its code is real. The off-by-one-day LLM date evidence comes from 2024 models and a single question type.

The researcher missed kzaremski/apple-notes-exporter (721 stars, v2.1 released 2026-09-15). It has a CLI with folder filtering, JSON/JSONL output, incremental sync and preserved dates, and it is the best ready-made alternative if Shane will grant Full Disk Access. Calendar events and email receipts are also a source of exact dates for lessons and equipment.

research.area: Golf analytics methodology (WHS, stats, lesson-impact inference) and overall app architecture
research.summary: Build a local-first Python app: ingest (screenshots, notes, manual/CSV) → SQLite with full provenance → a small FastAPI review/correct UI → a self-contained static HTML dashboard. An optional local MCP server can sit on top so Claude Desktop/Code can answer questions against golf.db. Most of the WHS math can be replicated exactly from the 2024 Rules of Handicapping, which I read in full. Differential = (113/Slope)×(AGS−CR−PCC). Net double bogey = par+2+strokes received. Handicap Index = average of the lowest 8 of the most recent 20 differentials. The old ×0.96 multiplier is gone, and there is a published table for 3–19 scores, soft/hard caps and exceptional-score reductions. Your own replica can't match the official one exactly: PCC needs at least 8 same-day scores from the field, and the 2024 'expected score' used for 9-hole and 10–17-hole rounds is unpublished. The only public approximation is an unofficial 0.52×HI+1.2, which does reproduce the USGA's worked example. For lesson impact the honest constraint is noise. Differential SD is about 3–3.5 strokes for mid-handicaps, so a 5-vs-5 round comparison can only detect changes of about 5–6 strokes, and 10 each side about 4. On top of that, lessons booked after a bad stretch show a spurious gain of about 2.2 strokes purely from regression to the mean (my simulation). My recommended primary method is a Bayesian segmented regression (interrupted time series) on course-normalised differentials: Student-t errors, a learning-dip window after each lesson, and partially pooled lesson effects. Back it up with in-time placebo tests and a local-level smoothed 'ability' line. The main visual is a differential timeline with lesson markers plus a forest plot of lesson effects. True strokes gained can't be computed without shot distances. What you can defend: an exact per-hole identity split (to-green vs putts), a coarse two-state (GIR / no GIR) strokes gained against your own baseline, 'stat-implied handicap' benchmarking against amateur benchmark tables, and per-hole mixed models that are explicitly associational. Default to never publishing notes or scores on GitHub Pages: Pages sites are public even when the repo is private. The simplest iPhone→Mac route is a Share-Sheet Shortcut that saves the screenshot to an iCloud Drive inbox, watched by a launchd agent. Two alternatives: a Shortcut that POSTs to a local FastAPI endpoint, or osxphotos pulling screenshots straight from the Photos library.

options.name: A. Local Python pipeline → SQLite → self-contained static HTML (CLI only)
options.how_it_works: `golf ingest ...` runs extractors (Claude vision for screenshots, Claude text for notes, CSV/manual), validates the results and writes them to SQLite. `golf build` renders one HTML file with the data embedded as JSON and charts inlined (Altair `chart.save(inline=True)` via vl-convert, or hand-rolled SVG like the Bell rent watch project). You fix extraction errors by editing a staged JSON/CSV and re-importing, or in Datasette.
options.data_obtained: Whatever the sources carry: hole-by-hole strokes, par, stroke index, putts, FIR (hit/L/R), GIR (app or derived), penalties, sand; round date, course and tees; CR/Slope entered manually per tee; events (lessons, practice, equipment) from notes.
options.effort: About 1–2 weekends for the MVP (WHS module, ingest, build).
options.risks: No comfortable correction loop: screenshot extraction will occasionally be wrong, and editing JSON is friction. Otherwise low risk because everything stays on the laptop.

evidence.claim: Altair can save fully offline HTML with the JS inlined (`chart.save('chart.html', inline=True)`), which needs vl-convert-python
Official 2024 Rules of Handicapping text (formulas used by the WHS module)

options.name: B. RECOMMENDED: hybrid of A plus a local FastAPI review/upload app
options.how_it_works: Same pipeline as A. `golf serve` adds a FastAPI + Jinja2/htmx app on localhost:8765 with: /upload (multipart, also the target for an iOS Shortcut), a review queue (screenshot on the left, editable 18-hole grid on the right, validator warnings highlighted, Confirm writes rounds/holes and logs field corrections), an events review (proposed events next to the highlighted source quote: accept, edit or reject), and /dashboard serving the built static page. The dashboard is still produced as one static file, so it can be opened offline or deployed.
options.data_obtained: Same as A, plus a human-verified status per round/event and a corrections log. The log doubles as a growing golden set for extraction evals.
options.effort: About 2–3 weekends for MVP, plus about 1 weekend for lesson modelling and timeline.
options.risks: A local server has to be running for uploads (use launchd or run it on demand). Keep it bound to localhost/LAN only; add a shared-secret header if exposing it on the LAN for the Shortcut. The Anthropic API key lives in .env and is never committed.

research.design_notes:
## 1. WHS engine (2024 Rules of Handicapping, effective Jan 2024; I found no newer revision as of Sep 2026)
Sources: the official Rules of Handicapping 2024. The USGA PDF returns 403 to fetch; I read the identical joint USGA/R&A text mirrored by GolfRSA, plus the R&A online Rules 3 and 5.

- **Score Differential (18 holes)** = (113 / Slope) × (AGS − CR − PCC). Round to 0.1 with .5 rounded up; negative values round toward 0 (−1.55 → −1.5). PCC ∈ {−1, 0, +1, +2, +3}.
  - PCC needs **at least 8 acceptable same-day scores** at the course, so your app can't compute it. Store `pcc=0` and label the result 'unofficial'.
  - If you post to GHIN, store GHIN's differential in `official_differential` and prefer it.
- **AGS / hole caps:**
  - Net double bogey = par + 2 + strokes received on the hole (from the full Course Handicap, rounded).
  - Before an initial HI exists (fewer than 54 holes): par + 5.
  - If Course Handicap > 54 and you receive 4 or more strokes on a hole: par + 5.
  - Picked-up hole: the lower of most-likely score and NDB.
  - Strokes received on a hole = floor(CH/18) + (SI ≤ CH mod 18). SI 1 repeats as 19, 37, 55.
  - 9-hole rounds on an 18-hole course take strokes in ascending order of the published 18-hole SIs (Appendix E).
- **Course Handicap** = HI × Slope/113 + (CR − Par), rounded at the end.
  - 9-hole: (HI/2, rounded to 0.1) × Slope9/113 + (CR9 − Par9).
  - For NDB, use the HI in effect **before** the round, so recompute chronologically.
- **9-hole rounds:** diff9 = (113/Slope9) × (AGS9 − CR9 − 0.5·PCC). The 18-hole differential = diff9 (unrounded) + the expected 9-hole differential for your HI, then rounded.
  - The expected-score formula is **not published**. The unofficial 0.52×HI + 1.2 (Golf Monthly forum, Apr 2024) reproduces the USGA/MGA example exactly: HI 14.0 gives 8.48, and 7.2 + 8.48 = 15.68 → 15.7.
  - 10–17 holes count as an 18-hole score, using the expected score for unplayed holes (also unpublished). Pro-rating 0.52×HI+1.2 per hole is my extrapolation and unverified.
  - Fewer than 9 holes: not acceptable.
- **Handicap Index** (all rounded to 0.1, max 54.0; needs 54 holes to establish). **No 0.96 multiplier**: the pre-WHS USGA formula was 0.96 × average of the best 10 of 20.

  | Differentials in record | Used | Adjustment |
  |---|---|---|
  | 3 | lowest 1 | −2.0 |
  | 4 | lowest 1 | −1.0 |
  | 5 | lowest 1 | 0 |
  | 6 | average of lowest 2 | −1.0 |
  | 7–8 | lowest 2 | 0 |
  | 9–11 | lowest 3 | 0 |
  | 12–14 | lowest 4 | 0 |
  | 15–16 | lowest 5 | 0 |
  | 17–18 | lowest 6 | 0 |
  | 19 | lowest 7 | 0 |
  | 20 | lowest 8 of most recent 20 | 0 |

- **Low HI** = the lowest HI in the 365 days before the date of the most recent score; it exists only after 20 scores.
- **Caps:** soft cap halves any increase beyond 3.0 above Low HI; hard cap limits the HI to at most Low HI + 5.0. There's no limit on decreases.
- **Exceptional score reduction:** a differential 7.0–9.9 below the HI in effect gives −1.0; 10.0 or more gives −2.0. The reduction is applied to each of the most recent 20 differentials and is cumulative.
- **Implementation:** a pure-function `whs/` package. Recompute the whole history on every write (n is small) into `handicap_history`.
- **Unit tests from the official examples:**
  - Initial HI from 15.3 / 15.2 / 16.6 → 13.2.
  - Six differentials whose lowest two average 38.4 → 37.4.
  - Rounding: −1.54 → −1.5, −1.56 → −1.6.
  - 9-hole: HI 14.0 with diff9 7.2 → 15.7.

## 2. Descriptive analytics from 18Birdies-level data
Store data at the hole level. Every rate gets a Wilson CI and a rolling-20 / EWMA trend (NIST: λ = 0.2–0.3 is typical).

- **Scoring:** gross, to-par, AGS, differential. Average to par on par 3 / 4 / 5 (hole-level means with CIs). Front vs back nine. First-3-holes 'warm-up' split.
- **Tee:** FIR% on par 4s and 5s, plus the L/R miss split.
- **Approach:** GIR% overall and by par. Derive GIR when missing: strokes − putts ≤ par − 2 (chip-ins and fringe putts break this, so flag rather than overwrite).
- **Putting:**
  - Putts/round, putts per GIR, putts on non-GIR holes, 3-putt rate, 1-putt rate.
  - Broadie: putts/round 'is not a pure measure of putting skill because it doesn't take into account putt distances', and putts per GIR has the same drawback because golfers who hit more greens putt from longer distances. Show these stats, but never label them 'putting skill'.
- **Short game:**
  - Scrambling% = share of missed-GIR holes finished in par or better (PGA Tour definition).
  - Sand-save%, if 18Birdies records greenside bunker shots (unconfirmed).
- **Damage control:**
  - Penalty strokes/round. Double-bogey-or-worse rate. Triple+ rate. NDB strokes removed (gross − AGS).
  - Blow-up anatomy: classify each double+ by precursor (penalty / missed FIR / missed GIR + failed scramble / 3-putt).
  - Hole-to-hole 'tilt': P(bogey+ | previous hole bogey+) vs base rate, with a within-round permutation test.
- **Consistency:** rolling-20 SD, IQR and MAD of differentials; share of strokes over par that came from the worst 3 holes.
- **Benchmark context:**
  - Bingham & Swartz (49 golfers, 1997): SD of differentials ≈ 2.74 + 0.053·HI, i.e. about 3.3 at HI 10 and about 3.5 at HI 15. Scores are roughly normal with a slightly long right tail (Scheid). Use Student-t likelihoods.
  - Under that model the mean differential ≈ HI + 0.93σ ≈ HI + 3 (my order-statistics simulation). Shot Scope's observed average score to par exceeds handicap by +0.8 to +4.0.
  - HI sampling noise alone ≈ 0.28σ ≈ 1 stroke, so don't read ±1 HI moves as change.
- **Stat-implied handicap profile:** interpolate each stat on benchmark curves and compare it to your HI to see what's holding you back.
  - Shot Scope ebook (~2020; handicaps 0/5/10/15/20/25): GIR 61/44/36/24/17/10%; FIR roughly flat at 46–50%; up-and-down 47→18%; putts 29.4→33.8; penalties 0.56→4.67.
  - Break X (Sept 2026, 3,788 rounds): GIR 56.8→18.7%; putts 31.3→37.0.
  - The two vendors disagree, so version-control benchmark CSVs with their source URLs and show which one is in use.

**Strokes-gained approximations:**
- **Defensible:**
  1. Exact per-hole identity: (score − par) = [(strokes − putts) − (par − 2)] + [putts − 2], i.e. 'to-green over regulation' vs 'putts over two', with penalties broken out.
  2. Coarse two-state strokes gained against a baseline B (your trailing 40 rounds, or a benchmark):
     - SG_long = E_B[score | par] − (par − 2) − E_B[strokes after regulation | GIR state]
     - SG_finish = E_B[strokes after regulation | GIR state] − (score − (par − 2))
     - These telescope exactly to E_B[score | par] − score. SG_finish can be split into putts vs non-putts on missed-GIR holes.
  3. A hole-level mixed model, score − par ~ par_type + FIR + GIR + penalties + (1 | round), to estimate 'strokes value of a GIR/FIR' for you. It's associational: FIR works partly through GIR, so the FIR coefficient conditional on GIR is only a direct effect.
- **Not defensible:** true SG categories (off-tee / approach / around-green / putting) without distances; 'putting skill' from putts counts; a GHIN-exact HI without PCC; PGA Tour baselines for an amateur. (Broadie's finding that the long game explains about two-thirds of score variability is for Tour pros only.)

## 3. Lesson-impact analysis
**Threats to validity:**
- **Noise.** Minimum detectable effect at 80% power, α = 0.05, = 2.8σ√(2/n):

  | Rounds each side | σ = 3.0 | σ = 3.5 |
  |---|---|---|
  | 5 | 5.3 | 6.2 |
  | 10 | 3.8 | 4.4 |
  | 20 | 2.7 | 3.1 |
  | 30 | 2.2 | 2.5 |

- **Regression to the mean / Ashenfelter dip.** In my simulation with zero true effect, booking a lesson after a worst-20% five-round stretch produces a 2.2-stroke naive 5-vs-5 'improvement'.
- **Learning ≠ performance** (Soderstrom & Bjork 2015): a post-lesson dip is plausible.
- **Other confounders:** seasonality or early-season rust; equipment changed at the same time as a lesson (not separable); course/tee mix (differentials normalise CR/Slope but not PCC); autocorrelation (Bernal et al. 2017).
- **9-hole rounds.** Do **not** use WHS-scaled 9-hole differentials as the outcome: half of each value is a function of the prior HI, which pulls results toward 'no change'. Use 2·diff9 with weight 0.5 instead.
- **Handicap Index.** Never use the HI (lagged best-8 'potential') as the outcome.

**Primary method: Bayesian segmented regression (interrupted time series) on per-round AGS differentials.**
- Model: y_r = α + β·t_r + Σ_k δ_k·1[t_r ≥ L_k + w] + Σ_k ω_k·1[L_k ≤ t_r < L_k + w] + γ·x_r + ε_r, with ε_r ~ Student-t(ν, 0, σ/√weight_r).
  - w = learning window, e.g. 14 days or 3 rounds.
  - x = early-season flag, home course, 9-hole flag, competition.
- Priors:
  - δ_k ~ N(μ_δ, τ), with μ_δ ~ N(0, 2) and τ ~ HalfNormal(1.5). Partial pooling gives μ_δ = your typical lesson effect.
  - β ~ N(0, 2 strokes/yr); σ ~ HalfNormal(5); ν ~ Gamma(2, 0.1).
- Report per lesson: posterior mean, 80% and 95% intervals, P(δ < 0), P(δ < −1), and the number of rounds on each side.
- Fit with PyMC; it takes seconds for n < 500. Cross-check with statsmodels OLS plus Newey–West HAC standard errors.
- If lessons are evenly spaced, drop the linear trend or use a local-level baseline instead, because trend and step effects become confounded.

**Robustness:**
- **In-time placebo:** re-estimate the step at every non-lesson date at least w away from real lessons; the p-value is the real effect's rank among the placebos (the in-time placebo idea from Abadie 2021).
- **Pre-dip sensitivity:** drop the 5 rounds just before each lesson from the baseline.
- **Changepoint:** an exact single-changepoint posterior (conjugate normal, enumerating τ; no MCMC) to check whether any shift lines up with a lesson. BOCPD (Adams & MacKay) or ruptures if you want online or multiple changepoints.
- **Bootstrap:** only BCa or t intervals. Percentile intervals under-cover at small n (Hesterberg); my simulation gave 88% coverage for a nominal 95% at 5 vs 5.

**Primary visual:**
- Differential timeline: dots, with the y-axis inverted so better is up, and 9-hole rounds hollow.
- A local-level (ETS(A,N,N) / UnobservedComponents) smoothed 'ability' line with an 80% band.
- A dashed step line for the WHS-style HI, labelled 'potential, unofficial'.
- Vertical labelled rules for lessons; lighter ticks for equipment changes; shaded spans for practice blocks and injuries.
- A companion forest plot of δ_k and μ_δ, with an MDE note ('with your σ, you need about 20 rounds each side to see 3 strokes').

Where do your golf notes live: Apple Notes (which folder?), markdown/Obsidian, Google Docs, or somewhere else? Do the notes usually carry explicit dates, or will relative dates like 'last Tuesday' need resolving?
Roughly how many rounds are in 18Birdies, how many lessons have you had, and how often do you play 9-hole rounds? This decides how much the lesson-impact analysis can actually detect.
Which 18Birdies screens would you screenshot (hole-by-hole scorecard vs round stats), and do you consistently log putts, fairways, GIR and penalties in the app?

Is a local-only dashboard OK, or do you want to see it on your phone? A public GitHub Pages site would expose your notes and scores; the alternatives are a stripped '--public' build or private hosting.
Is iCloud Photos syncing originals to this Mac? If so, the zero-touch 'pull screenshots from Photos' intake becomes possible.
Would you log practice sessions (date and minutes/focus) going forward? Practice volume is a major confounder when measuring lesson effects.
